property.description: Indicates whether the event succeeded or failed.

property.description: Additional details about the error. This may be a text description of the error or a system code that identifies the error.

property.description: Unique id for the element within a resource (for internal references). This may be any string value that does not contain spaces.

codeset.description: Indicator for type of action performed during the event that generated the event.

code.name: C

code.name: R
code.description: Read data, such as to print or display to a doctor.

code.name: U
code.description: Update data, such as revise patient information.

code.name: D
code.description: Delete items, such as a doctor master file record.

code.name: E
code.description: Perform a system or application function such as log-on, program execution or use of an objects method, or perform a query/search operation.

codeset.name: AuditEventSeverity

code.name: Emergency
code.description: System is unusable. e.g., This level should only be reported by infrastructure and should not be used by applications.

code.name: Alert
code.description: Notification should be sent to trigger action be taken. e.g., Loss of the primary network connection needing attention.

code.name: Critical
code.description: Critical conditions. e.g., A failure in the systems primary application that will reset automatically.

code.name: Error
code.description: Error conditions. e.g., An application has exceeded its file storage limit and attempts to write are failing.

code.name: Warning
code.description: Warning conditions. May indicate that an error will occur if action is not taken. e.g., A non-root file system has only 2GB remaining.

code.name: Notice
code.description: Notice messages. Normal but significant condition. Events that are unusual, but not error conditions.

code.name: Informational
code.description: Normal operational messages that require no action. e.g., An application has started, paused, or ended successfully.

code.name: Debug
code.description: Debug-level messages. Information useful to developers for debugging the application.

code.name: Allocated

code.name: Issued
code.description: The dispensed product has been picked up.

code.name: Unfulfilled
code.description: The dispense could not be completed.

code.name: Returned
code.description: The dispensed product was returned.

code.name: EnteredInError
code.description: The dispense was entered in error and therefore nullified.

code.name: Unknown
code.description: The authoring system does not know which of the status values applies for this dispense. Note: this concept is not to be used for other - one of the listed statuses is presumed to apply, its just not known which one.

resource.name: BodyStructure
resource.description: Record details about an anatomical structure. This resource may be used when a coded concept does not provide the necessary detail needed for the use case.

property.name: id
property.description: The logical id of the resource, as used in the URL for the resource. Once assigned, this value never changes.

property.name: meta
property.description: The metadata about the resource. This is content that is maintained by the infrastructure. Changes to the content might not always be associated with version changes to the resource.

property.name: implicitRules
property.description: A reference to a set of rules that were followed when the resource was constructed, and which must be understood when processing the content. Often, this is a reference to an implementation guide that defines the special rules along with other profiles etc.

property.name: language
property.description: The base language in which the resource is written.

property.name: text
property.description: A human-readable narrative that contains a summary of the resource and can be used to represent the content of the resource to a human. The narrative need not encode all the structured data, but is required to contain sufficient detail to make it "clinically safe" for a human to just read the narrative. Resource definitions may define what content should be represented in the narrative to ensure clinical safety.

property.name: identifier
property.description: Identifier for this instance of the anatomical structure.

property.name: active
property.description: Whether this body site is in active use.

property.name: morphology
property.description: The kind of structure being represented by the body structure at `BodyStructure.location`. This can define both normal and abnormal morphologies.

property.name: includedStructure
property.description: The anatomical location(s) or region(s) of the specimen, lesion, or body structure.

property.name: excludedStructure
property.description: The anatomical location(s) or region(s) not occupied or represented by the specimen, lesion, or body structure.

property.name: description
property.description: A summary, characterization or explanation of the body structure.

property.name: image
property.description: Image or images used to identify a location.

property.name: patient
property.description: The person to which the body site belongs.

property.name: id
property.description: Unique id for the element within a resource (for internal references). This may be any string value that does not contain spaces.

property.name: structure
property.description: Code that represents the included structure.

property.name: laterality
property.description: Code that represents the included structure laterality.

property.name: bodyLandmarkOrientation
property.description: Body locations in relation to a specific body landmark (tatoo, scar, other body structure).

property.name: spatialReference
property.description: XY or XYZ-coordinate orientation for structure.

property.name: qualifier
property.description: Code that represents the included structure qualifier.

property.name: id
property.description: Unique id for the element within a resource (for internal references). This may be any string value that does not contain spaces.

property.name: landmarkDescription
property.description: A description of a landmark on the body used as a reference to locate something else.

property.name: clockFacePosition
property.description: An description of the direction away from a landmark something is located based on a radial clock dial.

property.name: distanceFromLandmark
property.description: The distance in centimeters a certain observation is made from a body landmark.

property.name: surfaceOrientation
property.description: The surface area a body location is in relation to a landmark.

property.name: id
property.description: Unique id for the element within a resource (for internal references). This may be any string value that does not contain spaces.

property.name: device
property.description: An instrument, tool, analyzer, etc. used in the measurement.

property.name: value
property.description: The measured distance (e.g., in cm) from a body landmark.

resource.name: Bundle
resource.description: A container for a collection of resources.

property.name: id
property.description: The logical id of the resource, as used in the URL for the resource. Once assigned, this value never changes.

property.name: meta
property.description: The metadata about the resource. This is content that is maintained by the infrastructure. Changes to the content might not always be associated with version changes to the resource.

property.name: implicitRules
property.description: A reference to a set of rules that were followed when the resource was constructed, and which must be understood when processing the content. Often, this is a reference to an implementation guide that defines the special rules along with other profiles etc.

property.name: language
property.description: The base language in which the resource is written.

property.name: identifier
property.description: A persistent identifier for the bundle that wont change as a bundle is copied from server to server.

property.name: type
property.description: Indicates the purpose of this bundle - how it is intended to be used.

property.name: timestamp
property.description: The date/time that the bundle was assembled - i.e. when the resources were placed in the bundle.

property.name: total
property.description: If a set of search matches, this is the (potentially estimated) total number of entries of type match across all pages in the search. It does not include search.mode = include or outcome entries and it does not provide a count of the number of entries in the Bundle.

property.name: link
property.description: A series of links that provide context to this bundle.

property.name: entry
property.description: An entry in a bundle resource - will either contain a resource or information about a resource (transactions and history only).

property.name: signature
property.description: Digital Signature - base64 encoded. XML-DSig or a JWS.

property.name: issues
property.description: Captures issues and warnings that relate to the construction of the Bundle and the content within it.

property.name: id
property.description: Unique id for the element within a resource (for internal references). This may be any string value that does not contain spaces.

property.name: relation
property.description: A name which details the functional use for this link - see [http://www.iana.org/assignments/link-relations/link-relations.xhtml#link-relations-1](http://www.iana.org/assignments/link-relations/link-relations.xhtml#link-relations-1).

property.name: url
property.description: The reference details for the link.

property.name: id
property.description: Unique id for the element within a resource (for internal references). This may be any string value that does not contain spaces.

property.name: link
property.description: A series of links that provide context to this entry.

property.name: fullUrl
property.description: The Absolute URL for the resource. Except for transactions and batches, each entry in a Bundle must have a fullUrl. The fullUrl SHALL NOT disagree with the id in the resource - i.e. if the fullUrl is not a urn:uuid, the URL shall be version-independent URL consistent with the Resource.id. The fullUrl is a version independent reference to the resource. Even when not required, fullUrl MAY be set to a urn:uuid to allow referencing entries in a transaction. The fullUrl can be an arbitrary URI and is not limited to urn:uuid, urn:oid, http, and https. The fullUrl element SHALL have a value except when: * invoking a create* invoking or responding to an operation where the body is not a single identified resource* invoking or returning the results of a search or history operation.

property.name: resource
property.description: The Resource for the entry. The purpose/meaning of the resource is determined by the Bundle.type. This is allowed to be a Parameters resource if and only if it is referenced by something else within the Bundle that provides context/meaning.

property.name: search
property.description: Information about the search process that lead to the creation of this entry.

property.name: request
property.description: Additional information about how this entry should be processed as part of a transaction or batch. For history, it shows how the entry was processed to create the version contained in the entry.

property.name: response
property.description: Indicates the results of processing the corresponding request entry in the batch or transaction being responded to or what the results of an operation where when returning history.

property.name: id
property.description: Unique id for the element within a resource (for internal references). This may be any string value that does not contain spaces.

property.name: mode
property.description: Why this entry is in the result set - whether its included as a match or because of an _include requirement, or to convey information or warning information about the search process.

property.name: score
property.description: When searching, the servers search ranking score for the entry.

property.name: id
property.description: Unique id for the element within a resource (for internal references). This may be any string value that does not contain spaces.

property.name: method
property.description: In a transaction or batch, this is the HTTP action to be executed for this entry. In a history bundle, this indicates the HTTP action that occurred.

property.name: url
property.description: The URL for this entry, relative to the root (the address to which the request is posted).

property.name: ifNoneMatch
property.description: If the ETag values match, return a 304 Not Modified status. See the API documentation for ["Conditional Read"](http.html#cread).

property.name: ifModifiedSince
property.description: Only perform the operation if the last updated date matches. See the API documentation for ["Conditional Read"](http.html#cread).

property.name: ifMatch
property.description: Only perform the operation if the Etag value matches. For more information, see the API section ["Managing Resource Contention"](http.html#concurrency).

property.name: ifNoneExist
property.description: Instruct the server not to perform the create if a specified resource already exists. For further information, see the API documentation for ["Conditional Create"](http.html#ccreate). This is just the query portion of the URL - what follows the "?" (not including the "?").

property.name: id
property.description: Unique id for the element within a resource (for internal references). This may be any string value that does not contain spaces.

property.name: status
property.description: The status code returned by processing this entry. The status SHALL start with a 3 digit HTTP code (e.g. 404) and may contain the standard HTTP description associated with the status code.

property.name: location
property.description: The location header created by processing this operation, populated if the operation returns a location.

property.name: etag
property.description: The Etag for the resource, if the operation for the entry produced a versioned resource (see [Resource Metadata and Versioning](http.html#versioning) and [Managing Resource Contention](http.html#concurrency)).

property.name: lastModified
property.description: The date/time that the resource was modified on the server.

property.name: outcome
property.description: An OperationOutcome containing hints and warnings produced as part of processing this entry in a batch or transaction.

codeset.name: BundleType
codeset.description: Indicates the purpose of a bundle - how it is intended to be used.

code.name: Document
code.description: The bundle is a document. The first resource is a Composition.

code.name: Message
code.description: The bundle is a message. The first resource is a MessageHeader.

code.name: Transaction
code.description: The bundle is a transaction - intended to be processed by a server as an atomic commit.

code.name: TransactionResponse
code.description: The bundle is a transaction response. Because the response is a transaction response, the transaction has succeeded, and all responses are error free.

code.name: Batch
code.description: The bundle is a set of actions - intended to be processed by a server as a group of independent actions.

code.name: BatchResponse
code.description: The bundle is a batch response. Note that as a batch, some responses may indicate failure and others success.

code.name: History
code.description: The bundle is a list of resources from a history interaction on a server.

code.name: Searchset
code.description: The bundle is a list of resources returned as a result of a search/query interaction, operation, or message.

code.name: Collection
code.description: The bundle is a set of resources collected into a single package for ease of distribution that imposes no processing obligations or behavioral rules beyond persistence.

code.name: SubscriptionNotification
code.description: The bundle has been generated by a Subscription to communicate information to a client.

codeset.name: LinkRelationTypes
codeset.description: Link Relation Types defined at https://www.iana.org/assignments/link-relations/link-relations.xhtml#link-relations-1

code.name: About
code.description: Refers to a resource that is the subject of the links context.

code.name: Acl
code.description: Asserts that the link target provides an access control description for the link context.

code.name: Alternate
code.description: Refers to a substitute for this context

code.name: Amphtml
code.description: Used to reference alternative content that uses the AMP profile of the HTML format.

code.name: Appendix
code.description: Refers to an appendix.

code.name: AppleTouchIcon
code.description: Refers to an icon for the context. Synonym for icon.

code.name: AppleTouchStartupImage
code.description: Refers to a launch screen for the context.

code.name: Archives
code.description: Refers to a collection of records, documents, or other materials of historical interest.

code.name: Author
code.description: Refers to the contexts author.

code.name: BlockedBy
code.description: Identifies the entity that blocks access to a resource following receipt of a legal demand.

code.name: Bookmark
code.description: Gives a permanent link to use for bookmarking purposes.

code.name: Canonical
code.description: Designates the preferred version of a resource (the IRI and its contents).

code.name: Chapter
code.description: Refers to a chapter in a collection of resources.

code.name: CiteAs
code.description: Indicates that the link target is preferred over the link context for the purpose of permanent citation.

code.name: Collection
code.description: The target IRI points to a resource which represents the collection resource for the context IRI.

code.name: Contents
code.description: Refers to a table of contents.

code.name: ConvertedFrom
code.description: The document linked to was later converted to the document that contains this link relation. For example, an RFC can have a link to the Internet-Draft that became the RFC; in that case, the link relation would be "convertedFrom".

code.name: Copyright
code.description: Refers to a copyright statement that applies to the links context.

code.name: CreateForm
code.description: The target IRI points to a resource where a submission form can be obtained.

code.name: Current
code.description: Refers to a resource containing the most recent item(s) in a collection of resources.

code.name: Describedby
code.description: Refers to a resource providing information about the links context.

code.name: Describes
code.description: The relationship A describes B asserts that resource A provides a description of resource B. There are no constraints on the format or representation of either A or B, neither are there any further constraints on either resource.

code.name: Disclosure
code.description: Refers to a list of patent disclosures made with respect to material for which disclosure relation is specified.

code.name: DnsPrefetch
code.description: Used to indicate an origin that will be used to fetch required resources for the link context, and that the user agent ought to resolve as early as possible.

code.name: Duplicate
code.description: Refers to a resource whose available representations are byte-for-byte identical with the corresponding representations of the context IRI.

code.name: Edit
code.description: Refers to a resource that can be used to edit the links context.

code.name: EditForm
code.description: The target IRI points to a resource where a submission form for editing associated resource can be obtained.

code.name: EditMedia
code.description: Refers to a resource that can be used to edit media associated with the links context.

code.name: Enclosure
code.description: Identifies a related resource that is potentially large and might require special handling.

code.name: External
code.description: Refers to a resource that is not part of the same site as the current context.

code.name: First
code.description: An IRI that refers to the furthest preceding resource in a series of resources.

code.name: Glossary
code.description: Refers to a glossary of terms.

code.name: Help
code.description: Refers to context-sensitive help.

code.name: Hosts
code.description: Refers to a resource hosted by the server indicated by the link context.

code.name: Hub
code.description: Refers to a hub that enables registration for notification of updates to the context.

code.name: Icon
code.description: Refers to an icon representing the links context.

code.name: Index
code.description: Refers to an index.

code.name: IntervalAfter
code.description: refers to a resource associated with a time interval that ends before the beginning of the time interval associated with the context resource

code.name: IntervalBefore
code.description: refers to a resource associated with a time interval that begins after the end of the time interval associated with the context resource

code.name: IntervalContains
code.description: refers to a resource associated with a time interval that begins after the beginning of the time interval associated with the context resource, and ends before the end of the time interval associated with the context resource

code.name: IntervalDisjoint
code.description: refers to a resource associated with a time interval that begins after the end of the time interval associated with the context resource, or ends before the beginning of the time interval associated with the context resource

code.name: IntervalDuring
code.description: refers to a resource associated with a time interval that begins before the beginning of the time interval associated with the context resource, and ends after the end of the time interval associated with the context resource

code.name: IntervalEquals
code.description: refers to a resource associated with a time interval whose beginning coincides with the beginning of the time interval associated with the context resource, and whose end coincides with the end of the time interval associated with the context resource

code.name: IntervalFinishedBy
code.description: refers to a resource associated with a time interval that begins after the beginning of the time interval associated with the context resource, and whose end coincides with the end of the time interval associated with the context resource

code.name: IntervalFinishes
code.description: refers to a resource associated with a time interval that begins before the beginning of the time interval associated with the context resource, and whose end coincides with the end of the time interval associated with the context resource

code.name: IntervalIn
code.description: refers to a resource associated with a time interval that begins before or is coincident with the beginning of the time interval associated with the context resource, and ends after or is coincident with the end of the time interval associated with the context resource

code.name: IntervalMeets
code.description: refers to a resource associated with a time interval whose beginning coincides with the end of the time interval associated with the context resource

code.name: IntervalMetBy
code.description: refers to a resource associated with a time interval whose end coincides with the beginning of the time interval associated with the context resource

code.name: IntervalOverlappedBy
code.description: refers to a resource associated with a time interval that begins before the beginning of the time interval associated with the context resource, and ends after the beginning of the time interval associated with the context resource

code.name: IntervalOverlaps
code.description: refers to a resource associated with a time interval that begins before the end of the time interval associated with the context resource, and ends after the end of the time interval associated with the context resource

code.name: IntervalStartedBy
code.description: refers to a resource associated with a time interval whose beginning coincides with the beginning of the time interval associated with the context resource, and ends before the end of the time interval associated with the context resource

code.name: IntervalStarts
code.description: refers to a resource associated with a time interval whose beginning coincides with the beginning of the time interval associated with the context resource, and ends after the end of the time interval associated with the context resource

code.name: Item
code.description: The target IRI points to a resource that is a member of the collection represented by the context IRI.

code.name: Last
code.description: An IRI that refers to the furthest following resource in a series of resources.

code.name: LatestVersion
code.description: Points to a resource containing the latest (e.g., current) version of the context.

code.name: License
code.description: Refers to a license associated with this context.

code.name: Linkset
code.description: The link target of a link with the "linkset" relation type provides a set of links, including links in which the link context of the link participates.

code.name: Lrdd
code.description: Refers to further information about the links context, expressed as a LRDD ("Link-based Resource Descriptor Document") resource. See for information about processing this relation type in host-meta documents. When used elsewhere, it refers to additional links and other metadata. Multiple instances indicate additional LRDD resources. LRDD resources MUST have an "application/xrd+xml" representation, and MAY have others.

code.name: Manifest
code.description: Links to a manifest file for the context.

code.name: MaskIcon
code.description: Refers to a mask that can be applied to the icon for the context.

code.name: MediaFeed
code.description: Refers to a feed of personalised media recommendations relevant to the link context.

code.name: Memento
code.description: The Target IRI points to a Memento, a fixed resource that will not change state anymore.

code.name: Micropub
code.description: Links to the contexts Micropub endpoint.

code.name: Modulepreload
code.description: Refers to a module that the user agent is to preemptively fetch and store for use in the current context.

code.name: Monitor
code.description: Refers to a resource that can be used to monitor changes in an HTTP resource.

code.name: MonitorGroup
code.description: Refers to a resource that can be used to monitor changes in a specified group of HTTP resources.

code.name: Next
code.description: Indicates that the links context is a part of a series, and that the next in the series is the link target.

code.name: NextArchive
code.description: Refers to the immediately following archive resource.

code.name: Nofollow
code.description: Indicates that the contexts original author or publisher does not endorse the link target.

code.name: Noopener
code.description: Indicates that any newly created top-level browsing context which results from following the link will not be an auxiliary browsing context.

code.name: Noreferrer
code.description: Indicates that no referrer information is to be leaked when following the link.

code.name: Opener
code.description: Indicates that any newly created top-level browsing context which results from following the link will be an auxiliary browsing context.

code.name: Openid2_local_id
code.description: Refers to an OpenID Authentication server on which the context relies for an assertion that the end user controls an Identifier.

code.name: Openid2_provider
code.description: Refers to a resource which accepts OpenID Authentication protocol messages for the context.

code.name: Original
code.description: The Target IRI points to an Original Resource.

code.name: P3Pv1
code.description: Refers to a P3P privacy policy for the context.

code.name: Payment
code.description: Indicates a resource where payment is accepted.

code.name: Pingback
code.description: Gives the address of the pingback resource for the link context.

code.name: Preconnect
code.description: Used to indicate an origin that will be used to fetch required resources for the link context. Initiating an early connection, which includes the DNS lookup, TCP handshake, and optional TLS negotiation, allows the user agent to mask the high latency costs of establishing a connection.

code.name: PredecessorVersion
code.description: Points to a resource containing the predecessor version in the version history.

code.name: Prefetch
code.description: The prefetch link relation type is used to identify a resource that might be required by the next navigation from the link context, and that the user agent ought to fetch, such that the user agent can deliver a faster response once the resource is requested in the future.

code.name: Preload
code.description: Refers to a resource that should be loaded early in the processing of the links context, without blocking rendering.

code.name: Prerender
code.description: Used to identify a resource that might be required by the next navigation from the link context, and that the user agent ought to fetch and execute, such that the user agent can deliver a faster response once the resource is requested in the future.

code.name: Prev
code.description: Indicates that the links context is a part of a series, and that the previous in the series is the link target.

code.name: Preview
code.description: Refers to a resource that provides a preview of the links context.

code.name: Previous
code.description: Refers to the previous resource in an ordered series of resources. Synonym for "prev".

code.name: PrevArchive
code.description: Refers to the immediately preceding archive resource.

code.name: PrivacyPolicy
code.description: Refers to a privacy policy associated with the links context.

code.name: Profile
code.description: Identifying that a resource representation conformsto a certain profile, without affecting the non-profile semanticsof the resource representation.

code.name: Publication
code.description: Links to a publication manifest. A manifest represents structured information about a publication, such as informative metadata, a list of resources, and a default reading order.

code.name: Related
code.description: Identifies a related resource.

code.name: Restconf
code.description: Identifies the root of RESTCONF API as configured on this HTTP server. The "restconf" relation defines the root of the API defined in RFC8040. Subsequent revisions of RESTCONF will use alternate relation values to support protocol versioning.

code.name: Replies
code.description: Identifies a resource that is a reply to the context of the link.

code.name: Ruleinput
code.description: The resource identified by the link target provides an input value to an instance of a rule, where the resource which represents the rule instance is identified by the link context.

code.name: Search
code.description: Refers to a resource that can be used to search through the links context and related resources.

code.name: Section
code.description: Refers to a section in a collection of resources.

code.name: Self
code.description: Conveys an identifier for the links context.

code.name: Service
code.description: Indicates a URI that can be used to retrieve a service document.

code.name: ServiceDesc
code.description: Identifies service description for the context that is primarily intended for consumption by machines.

code.name: ServiceDoc
code.description: Identifies service documentation for the context that is primarily intended for human consumption.

code.name: ServiceMeta
code.description: Identifies general metadata for the context that is primarily intended for consumption by machines.

code.name: Sponsored
code.description: Refers to a resource that is within a context that is sponsored (such as advertising or another compensation agreement).

code.name: Start
code.description: Refers to the first resource in a collection of resources.

code.name: Status
code.description: Identifies a resource that represents the contexts status.

code.name: Stylesheet
code.description: Refers to a stylesheet.

code.name: Subsection
code.description: Refers to a resource serving as a subsection in a collection of resources.

code.name: SuccessorVersion
code.description: Points to a resource containing the successor version in the version history.

code.name: Sunset
code.description: Identifies a resource that provides information about the contexts retirement policy.

code.name: Tag
code.description: Gives a tag (identified by the given address) that applies to the current document.

code.name: TermsOfService
code.description: Refers to the terms of service associated with the links context.

code.name: Timegate
code.description: The Target IRI points to a TimeGate for an Original Resource.

code.name: Timemap
code.description: The Target IRI points to a TimeMap for an Original Resource.

code.name: Type
code.description: Refers to a resource identifying the abstract semantic type of which the links context is considered to be an instance.

code.name: Ugc
code.description: Refers to a resource that is within a context that is User Generated Content.

code.name: Up
code.description: Refers to a parent document in a hierarchy of documents.

code.name: VersionHistory
code.description: Points to a resource containing the version history for the context.

code.name: Via
code.description: Identifies a resource that is the source of the information in the links context.

code.name: Webmention
code.description: Identifies a target URI that supports the Webmention protocol. This allows clients that mention a resource in some form of publishing process to contact that endpoint and inform it that this resource has been mentioned.

code.name: WorkingCopy
code.description: Points to a working copy for this resource.

code.name: WorkingCopyOf
code.description: Points to the versioned resource from which this working copy was obtained.

codeset.name: SearchEntryMode
codeset.description: Why an entry is in the result set - whether its included as a match or because of an _include requirement, or to convey information or warning information about the search process.

code.name: Match
code.description: This resource matched the search specification.

code.name: Include
code.description: This resource is returned because it is referred to from another resource in the search set.

code.name: Outcome
code.description: An OperationOutcome that provides additional information about the processing of a search.

codeset.name: HTTPVerb
codeset.description: HTTP verbs (in the HTTP command line). See [HTTP rfc](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7231) for details.

code.name: GET
code.description: HTTP GET Command.

code.name: HEAD
code.description: HTTP HEAD Command.

code.name: POST
code.description: HTTP POST Command.

code.name: PUT
code.description: HTTP PUT Command.

code.name: DELETE
code.description: HTTP DELETE Command.

code.name: PATCH
code.description: HTTP PATCH Command.

resource.name: CapabilityStatement
resource.description: A Capability Statement documents a set of capabilities (behaviors) of a FHIR Server or Client for a particular version of FHIR that may be used as a statement of actual server functionality or a statement of required or desired server implementation.

property.name: id
property.description: The logical id of the resource, as used in the URL for the resource. Once assigned, this value never changes.

property.name: meta
property.description: The metadata about the resource. This is content that is maintained by the infrastructure. Changes to the content might not always be associated with version changes to the resource.

property.name: implicitRules
property.description: A reference to a set of rules that were followed when the resource was constructed, and which must be understood when processing the content. Often, this is a reference to an implementation guide that defines the special rules along with other profiles etc.

property.name: language
property.description: The base language in which the resource is written.

property.name: text
property.description: A human-readable narrative that contains a summary of the resource and can be used to represent the content of the resource to a human. The narrative need not encode all the structured data, but is required to contain sufficient detail to make it "clinically safe" for a human to just read the narrative. Resource definitions may define what content should be represented in the narrative to ensure clinical safety.

property.name: url
property.description: An absolute URI that is used to identify this capability statement when it is referenced in a specification, model, design or an instance; also called its canonical identifier. This SHOULD be globally unique and SHOULD be a literal address at which an authoritative instance of this capability statement is (or will be) published. This URL can be the target of a canonical reference. It SHALL remain the same when the capability statement is stored on different servers.

property.name: identifier
property.description: A formal identifier that is used to identify this CapabilityStatement when it is represented in other formats, or referenced in a specification, model, design or an instance.

property.name: version
property.description: The identifier that is used to identify this version of the capability statement when it is referenced in a specification, model, design or instance. This is an arbitrary value managed by the capability statement author and is not expected to be globally unique. For example, it might be a timestamp (e.g. yyyymmdd) if a managed version is not available. There is also no expectation that versions can be placed in a lexicographical sequence.

property.name: versionAlgorithm
property.description: Indicates the mechanism used to compare versions to determine which is more current.

property.name: name
property.description: A natural language name identifying the capability statement. This name should be usable as an identifier for the module by machine processing applications such as code generation.

property.name: title
property.description: A short, descriptive, user-friendly title for the capability statement.

property.name: status
property.description: The status of this capability statement. Enables tracking the life-cycle of the content.

property.name: experimental
property.description: A Boolean value to indicate that this capability statement is authored for testing purposes (or education/evaluation/marketing) and is not intended to be used for genuine usage.

property.name: date
property.description: The date (and optionally time) when the capability statement was last significantly changed. The date must change when the business version changes and it must change if the status code changes. In addition, it should change when the substantive content of the capability statement changes.

property.name: publisher
property.description: The name of the organization or individual responsible for the release and ongoing maintenance of the capability statement.

property.name: contact
property.description: Contact details to assist a user in finding and communicating with the publisher.

property.name: description
property.description: A free text natural language description of the capability statement from a consumers perspective. Typically, this is used when the capability statement describes a desired rather than an actual solution, for example as a formal expression of requirements as part of an RFP.

property.name: useContext
property.description: The content was developed with a focus and intent of supporting the contexts that are listed. These contexts may be general categories (gender, age, ...) or may be references to specific programs (insurance plans, studies, ...) and may be used to assist with indexing and searching for appropriate capability statement instances.

property.name: jurisdiction
property.description: A legal or geographic region in which the capability statement is intended to be used.

property.name: purpose
property.description: Explanation of why this capability statement is needed and why it has been designed as it has.

property.name: copyright
property.description: A copyright statement relating to the capability statement and/or its contents. Copyright statements are generally legal restrictions on the use and publishing of the capability statement.

property.name: copyrightLabel
property.description: A short string (lower than50 characters), suitable for inclusion in a page footer that identifies the copyright holder, effective period, and optionally whether rights are resctricted. (e.g. All rights reserved, Some rights reserved).

property.name: kind
property.description: The way that this statement is intended to be used, to describe an actual running instance of software, a particular product (kind, not instance of software) or a class of implementation (e.g. a desired purchase).

property.name: instantiates
property.description: Reference to a canonical URL of another CapabilityStatement that this software implements. This capability statement is a published API description that corresponds to a business service. The server may actually implement a subset of the capability statement it claims to implement, so the capability statement must specify the full capability details.

property.name: imports
property.description: Reference to a canonical URL of another CapabilityStatement that this software adds to. The capability statement automatically includes everything in the other statement, and it is not duplicated, though the server may repeat the same resources, interactions and operations to add additional details to them.

property.name: software
property.description: Software that is covered by this capability statement. It is used when the capability statement describes the capabilities of a particular software version, independent of an installation.

property.name: implementation
property.description: Identifies a specific implementation instance that is described by the capability statement - i.e. a particular installation, rather than the capabilities of a software program.

property.name: fhirVersion
property.description: The version of the FHIR specification that this CapabilityStatement describes (which SHALL be the same as the FHIR version of the CapabilityStatement itself). There is no default value.

property.name: format
property.description: A list of the formats supported by this implementation using their content types.

property.name: patchFormat
property.description: A list of the patch formats supported by this implementation using their content types.

property.name: acceptLanguage
property.description: A list of the languages supported by this implementation that are usefully supported in the ```Accept-Language``` header.

property.name: implementationGuide
property.description: A list of implementation guides that the server does (or should) support in their entirety.

property.name: rest
property.description: A definition of the restful capabilities of the solution, if any.

property.name: messaging
property.description: A description of the messaging capabilities of the solution.

property.name: document
property.description: A document definition.

property.name: id
property.description: Unique id for the element within a resource (for internal references). This may be any string value that does not contain spaces.

property.name: name
property.description: Name the software is known by.

property.name: version
property.description: The version identifier for the software covered by this statement.

property.name: releaseDate
property.description: Date this version of the software was released.

property.name: id
property.description: Unique id for the element within a resource (for internal references). This may be any string value that does not contain spaces.

property.name: description
property.description: Information about the specific installation that this capability statement relates to.

property.name: url
property.description: An absolute base URL for the implementation. This forms the base for REST interfaces as well as the mailbox and document interfaces.

property.name: custodian
property.description: The organization responsible for the management of the instance and oversight of the data on the server at the specified URL.

property.name: id
property.description: Unique id for the element within a resource (for internal references). This may be any string value that does not contain spaces.

property.name: mode
property.description: Identifies whether this portion of the statement is describing the ability to initiate or receive restful operations.

property.name: documentation
property.description: Information about the systems restful capabilities that apply across all applications, such as security.

property.name: security
property.description: Information about security implementation from an interface perspective - what a client needs to know.

property.name: resource
property.description: A specification of the restful capabilities of the solution for a specific resource type.

property.name: interaction
property.description: A specification of restful operations supported by the system.

property.name: searchParam
property.description: Search parameters that are supported for searching all resources for implementations to support and/or make use of - either references to ones defined in the specification, or additional ones defined for/by the implementation. This is only for searches executed against the system-level endpoint.

property.name: operation
property.description: Definition of an operation or a named query together with its parameters and their meaning and type.

property.name: compartment
property.description: An absolute URI which is a reference to the definition of a compartment that the system supports. The reference is to a CompartmentDefinition resource by its canonical URL .

property.name: id
property.description: Unique id for the element within a resource (for internal references). This may be any string value that does not contain spaces.

property.name: cors
property.description: Server adds CORS headers when responding to requests - this enables Javascript applications to use the server.

property.name: service
property.description: Types of security services that are supported/required by the system.

property.name: description
property.description: General description of how security works.

property.name: id
property.description: Unique id for the element within a resource (for internal references). This may be any string value that does not contain spaces.

property.name: type
property.description: A type of resource exposed via the restful interface.

property.name: profile
property.description: A system-wide profile that is applied across *all* instances of the resource supported by the system. For example, if declared on Observation, this profile is the "superset" of capabilities for laboratory *and* vitals *and* other domains. See further discussion in [Using Profiles](profiling.html#profile-uses).

property.name: supportedProfile
property.description: A list of profiles representing different use cases the system hosts/produces. A supported profile is a statement about the functionality of the data and services provided by the server (or the client) for supported use cases. For example, a system can define and declare multiple Observation profiles for laboratory observations, vital sign observations, etc. By declaring supported profiles, systems provide a way to determine whether individual resources are conformant. See further discussion in [Using Profiles](profiling.html#profile-uses).

property.name: documentation
property.description: Additional information about the resource type used by the system.

property.name: interaction
property.description: Identifies a restful operation supported by the solution.

property.name: versioning
property.description: This field is set to no-version to specify that the system does not support (server) or use (client) versioning for this resource type. If this has some other value, the server must at least correctly track and populate the versionId meta-property on resources. If the value is versioned-update, then the server supports all the versioning features, including using e-tags for version integrity in the API.

property.name: readHistory
property.description: A flag for whether the server is able to return past versions as part of the vRead operation.

property.name: updateCreate
property.description: A flag to indicate that the server allows or needs to allow the client to create new identities on the server (that is, the client PUTs to a location where there is no existing resource). Allowing this operation means that the server allows the client to create new identities on the server.

property.name: conditionalCreate
property.description: A flag that indicates that the server supports conditional create.

property.name: conditionalRead
property.description: A code that indicates how the server supports conditional read.

property.name: conditionalUpdate
property.description: A flag that indicates that the server supports conditional update.

property.name: conditionalPatch
property.description: A flag that indicates that the server supports conditional patch.

property.name: conditionalDelete
property.description: A code that indicates how the server supports conditional delete.

property.name: referencePolicy
property.description: A set of flags that defines how references are supported.

property.name: searchInclude
property.description: A list of _include values supported by the server.

property.name: searchRevInclude
property.description: A list of _revinclude (reverse include) values supported by the server.

property.name: searchParam
property.description: Search parameters for implementations to support and/or make use of - either references to ones defined in the specification, or additional ones defined for/by the implementation.

property.name: operation
property.description: Definition of an operation or a named query together with its parameters and their meaning and type. Consult the definition of the operation for details about how to invoke the operation, and the parameters.

property.name: id
property.description: Unique id for the element within a resource (for internal references). This may be any string value that does not contain spaces.

property.name: code
property.description: Coded identifier of the operation, supported by the system resource.

property.name: documentation
property.description: Guidance specific to the implementation of this operation, such as delete is a logical delete or updates are only allowed with version id or creates permitted from pre-authorized certificates only.

property.name: id
property.description: Unique id for the element within a resource (for internal references). This may be any string value that does not contain spaces.

property.name: name
property.description: The label used for the search parameter in this particular systems API - i.e. the name portion of the name-value pair that will appear as part of the search URL. This SHOULD be the same as the SearchParameter.code of the defining SearchParameter. However, it can sometimes differ if necessary to disambiguate when a server supports multiple SearchParameters that happen to share the same code.

property.name: definition
property.description: An absolute URI that is a formal reference to where this parameter was first defined, so that a client can be confident of the meaning of the search parameter (a reference to [SearchParameter.url](searchparameter-definitions.html#SearchParameter.url)). This element SHALL be populated if the search parameter refers to a SearchParameter defined by the FHIR core specification or externally defined IGs.

property.name: type
property.description: The type of value a search parameter refers to, and how the content is interpreted.

property.name: documentation
property.description: This allows documentation of any distinct behaviors about how the search parameter is used. For example, text matching algorithms.

property.name: id
property.description: Unique id for the element within a resource (for internal references). This may be any string value that does not contain spaces.

property.name: name
property.description: The name of the operation or query. For an operation, this name is prefixed with $ and used in the URL. For a query, this is the name used in the _query parameter when the query is called. This SHOULD be the same as the OperationDefinition.code of the defining OperationDefinition. However, it can sometimes differ if necessary to disambiguate when a server supports multiple OperationDefinition that happen to share the same code.

property.name: definition
property.description: Where the formal definition can be found. If a server references the base definition of an Operation (i.e. from the specification itself such as ```http://hl7.org/fhir/OperationDefinition/ValueSet-expand```), that means it supports the full capabilities of the operation - e.g. both GET and POST invocation. If it only supports a subset, it must define its own custom [OperationDefinition](operationdefinition.html#) with a base of the original OperationDefinition. The custom definition would describe the specific subset of functionality supported.

property.name: documentation
property.description: Documentation that describes anything special about the operation behavior, possibly detailing different behavior for system, type and instance-level invocation of the operation.

property.name: id
property.description: Unique id for the element within a resource (for internal references). This may be any string value that does not contain spaces.

property.name: code
property.description: A coded identifier of the operation, supported by the system.

property.name: documentation
property.description: Guidance specific to the implementation of this operation, such as limitations on the kind of transactions allowed, or information about system wide search is implemented.

property.name: id
property.description: Unique id for the element within a resource (for internal references). This may be any string value that does not contain spaces.

property.name: endpoint
property.description: An endpoint (network accessible address) to which messages and/or replies are to be sent.

property.name: reliableCache
property.description: Length if the receivers reliable messaging cache in minutes (if a receiver) or how long the cache length on the receiver should be (if a sender).

property.name: documentation
property.description: Documentation about the systems messaging capabilities for this endpoint not otherwise documented by the capability statement. For example, the process for becoming an authorized messaging exchange partner.

property.name: supportedMessage
property.description: References to message definitions for messages this system can send or receive.

property.name: id
property.description: Unique id for the element within a resource (for internal references). This may be any string value that does not contain spaces.

property.name: protocol
property.description: A list of the messaging transport protocol(s) identifiers, supported by this endpoint.

property.name: address
property.description: The network address of the endpoint. For solutions that do not use network addresses for routing, it can be just an identifier.

property.name: id
property.description: Unique id for the element within a resource (for internal references). This may be any string value that does not contain spaces.

property.name: mode
property.description: The mode of this event declaration - whether application is sender or receiver.

property.name: definition
property.description: Points to a message definition that identifies the messaging event, message structure, allowed responses, etc.

property.name: id
property.description: Unique id for the element within a resource (for internal references). This may be any string value that does not contain spaces.

property.name: mode
property.description: Mode of this document declaration - whether an application is a producer or consumer.

property.name: documentation
property.description: A description of how the application supports or uses the specified document profile. For example, when documents are created, what action is taken with consumed documents, etc.

property.name: profile
property.description: A profile on the document Bundle that constrains which resources are present, and their contents.

codeset.name: RestfulCapabilityMode
codeset.description: The mode of a RESTful capability statement.

code.name: Client
code.description: The application acts as a client for this resource.

code.name: Server
code.description: The application acts as a server for this resource.

codeset.name: TypeRestfulInteraction
codeset.description: Operations supported by REST at the type or instance level.

codeset.name: ResourceVersionPolicy
codeset.description: How the system supports versioning for a resource.

code.name: NoVersion
code.description: VersionId meta-property is not supported (server) or used (client).

code.name: Versioned
code.description: VersionId meta-property is supported (server) or used (client).

code.name: VersionedUpdate
code.description: Supports version-aware updates (server) or will be specified (If-match header) for updates (client).

codeset.name: ConditionalReadStatus
codeset.description: A code that indicates how the server supports conditional read.

code.name: NotSupported
code.description: No support for conditional reads.

code.name: ModifiedSince
code.description: Conditional reads are supported, but only with the If-Modified-Since HTTP Header.

code.name: NotMatch
code.description: Conditional reads are supported, but only with the If-None-Match HTTP Header.

code.name: FullSupport
code.description: Conditional reads are supported, with both If-Modified-Since and If-None-Match HTTP Headers.

codeset.name: ConditionalDeleteStatus
codeset.description: A code that indicates how the server supports conditional delete.

code.name: NotSupported
code.description: No support for conditional deletes.

code.name: Single
code.description: Conditional deletes are supported, but only single resources at a time.

code.name: Multiple
code.description: Conditional deletes are supported, and multiple resources can be deleted in a single interaction.

codeset.name: ReferenceHandlingPolicy
codeset.description: A set of flags that defines how references are supported.

code.name: Literal
code.description: The server supports and populates Literal references (i.e. using Reference.reference) where they are known (this code does not guarantee that all references are literal; see enforced).

code.name: Logical
code.description: The server allows logical references (i.e. using Reference.identifier).

code.name: Resolves
code.description: The server will attempt to resolve logical references to literal references - i.e. converting Reference.identifier to Reference.reference (if resolution fails, the server may still accept resources; see logical).

code.name: Enforced
code.description: The server enforces that references have integrity - e.g. it ensures that references can always be resolved. This is typically the case for clinical record systems, but often not the case for middleware/proxy systems.

code.name: Local
code.description: The server does not support references that point to other servers.

codeset.name: SystemRestfulInteraction
codeset.description: Operations supported by REST at the system level.

codeset.name: EventCapabilityMode
codeset.description: The mode of a message capability statement.

code.name: Sender
code.description: The application sends requests and receives responses.

code.name: Receiver
code.description: The application receives requests and sends responses.

codeset.name: DocumentMode
codeset.description: Whether the application produces or consumes documents.

code.name: Producer
code.description: The application produces documents of the specified type.

code.name: Consumer
code.description: The application consumes documents of the specified type.

operation.name: conforms
operation.description: This operation asks the server to check that it implements all the resources, interactions, search parameters, and operations that the client provides in its capability statement. The client provides both capability statements by reference, and must ensure that all the referenced resources are available to the conformance server

parameter.name: left
parameter.description: A canonical reference to the left-hand systems capability statement

parameter.name: right
parameter.description: A canonical reference to the right-hand systems capability statement

parameter.name: mode
parameter.description: What kind of comparison to perform - server to server, or client to server (use the codes server/server or client/server)

parameter.name: issues
parameter.description: Outcome of the CapabilityStatement test

parameter.name: union
parameter.description: The intersection of the functionality described by the CapabilityStatement resources

parameter.name: intersection
parameter.description: The union of the functionality described by the CapabilityStatement resources

operation.name: implements
operation.description: This operation asks the server to check that it implements all the resources, interactions, search parameters, and operations that the client provides in its capability statement. The client provides its capability statement inline, or by referring the server to the canonical URL of its capability statement

parameter.name: server
parameter.description: A canonical reference to the server capability statement - use this if the implements is not invoked on an instance (or on the /metadata end-point)

parameter.name: client
parameter.description: A canonical reference to the client capability statement - use this if the implements is not invoked on an instance (or on the /metadata end-point)

parameter.name: resource
parameter.description: The client capability statement, provided inline

parameter.name: return
parameter.description: Outcome of the CapabilityStatement test

operation.name: subset
operation.description: This operation asks the server to return a subset of the CapabilityStatement resource - just the REST parts that relate to a set of nominated resources - the resources that the client is interested in

parameter.name: server
parameter.description: The canonical URL - use this if the subset is not invoked on an instance (or on the /metadata end-point)

parameter.name: resource
parameter.description: A resource that the client would like to include in the return

parameter.name: return
parameter.description: The subsetted CapabilityStatement resource that is returned. This should be tagged with the SUBSETTED code

operation.name: versions
operation.description: Using the [FHIR Version Mime Type Parameter](http.html#version-parameter), a server can support [multiple versions on the same end-point](versioning.html#mt-version). The only way for client to find out what versions a server supports in this fashion is the $versions operation. The client invokes the operation with no parameters. and the server returns the list of supported versions, along with the default version it will use if no fhirVersion parameter is present

parameter.name: version
parameter.description: A version supported by the server. Use the major.minor version like 3.0

parameter.name: default
parameter.description: The default version for the server. Use the major.minor version like 3.0

resource.name: CarePlan
resource.description: Describes the intention of how one or more practitioners intend to deliver care for a particular patient, group or community for a period of time, possibly limited to care for a specific condition or set of conditions.

property.name: id
property.description: The logical id of the resource, as used in the URL for the resource. Once assigned, this value never changes.

property.name: meta
property.description: The metadata about the resource. This is content that is maintained by the infrastructure. Changes to the content might not always be associated with version changes to the resource.

property.name: implicitRules
property.description: A reference to a set of rules that were followed when the resource was constructed, and which must be understood when processing the content. Often, this is a reference to an implementation guide that defines the special rules along with other profiles etc.

property.name: language
property.description: The base language in which the resource is written.

property.name: text
property.description: A human-readable narrative that contains a summary of the resource and can be used to represent the content of the resource to a human. The narrative need not encode all the structured data, but is required to contain sufficient detail to make it "clinically safe" for a human to just read the narrative. Resource definitions may define what content should be represented in the narrative to ensure clinical safety.

property.name: identifier
property.description: Business identifiers assigned to this care plan by the performer or other systems which remain constant as the resource is updated and propagates from server to server.

property.name: instantiatesCanonical
property.description: The URL pointing to a FHIR-defined protocol, guideline, questionnaire or other definition that is adhered to in whole or in part by this CarePlan.

property.name: instantiatesUri
property.description: The URL pointing to an externally maintained protocol, guideline, questionnaire or other definition that is adhered to in whole or in part by this CarePlan.

property.name: basedOn
property.description: A higher-level request resource (i.e. a plan, proposal or order) that is fulfilled in whole or in part by this care plan.

property.name: replaces
property.description: Completed or terminated care plan whose function is taken by this new care plan.

property.name: partOf
property.description: A larger care plan of which this particular care plan is a component or step.

property.name: status
property.description: Indicates whether the plan is currently being acted upon, represents future intentions or is now a historical record.

property.name: intent
property.description: Indicates the level of authority/intentionality associated with the care plan and where the care plan fits into the workflow chain.

property.name: category
property.description: Identifies what "kind" of plan this is to support differentiation between multiple co-existing plans; e.g. "Home health", "psychiatric", "asthma", "disease management", "wellness plan", etc.

property.name: title
property.description: Human-friendly name for the care plan.

property.name: description
property.description: A description of the scope and nature of the plan.

property.name: subject
property.description: Identifies the patient or group whose intended care is described by the plan.

property.name: encounter
property.description: The Encounter during which this CarePlan was created or to which the creation of this record is tightly associated.

property.name: period
property.description: Indicates when the plan did (or is intended to) come into effect and end.

property.name: created
property.description: Represents when this particular CarePlan record was created in the system, which is often a system-generated date.

property.name: custodian
property.description: When populated, the custodian is responsible for the care plan. The care plan is attributed to the custodian.

property.name: contributor
property.description: Identifies the individual(s), organization or device who provided the contents of the care plan.

property.name: careTeam
property.description: Identifies all people and organizations who are expected to be involved in the care envisioned by this plan.

property.name: addresses
property.description: Identifies the conditions/problems/concerns/diagnoses/etc. whose management and/or mitigation are handled by this plan.

property.name: supportingInfo
property.description: Identifies portions of the patients record that specifically influenced the formation of the plan. These might include comorbidities, recent procedures, limitations, recent assessments, etc.

property.name: goal
property.description: Describes the intended objective(s) of carrying out the care plan.

property.name: activity
property.description: Identifies an action that has occurred or is a planned action to occur as part of the plan. For example, a medication to be used, lab tests to perform, self-monitoring that has occurred, education etc.

property.name: note
property.description: General notes about the care plan not covered elsewhere.

property.name: id
property.description: Unique id for the element within a resource (for internal references). This may be any string value that does not contain spaces.

property.name: performedActivity
property.description: Identifies the activity that was performed. For example, an activity could be patient education, exercise, or a medication administration. The reference to an "event" resource, such as Procedure or Encounter or Observation, represents the activity that was performed. The requested activity can be conveyed using the CarePlan.activity.plannedActivityReference (a reference to a request resource).

property.name: progress
property.description: Notes about the adherence/status/progress of the activity.

property.name: plannedActivityReference
property.description: The details of the proposed activity represented in a specific resource.

codeset.name: CarePlanIntent
codeset.description: Codes indicating the degree of authority/intentionality associated with a care plan.

resource.name: CareTeam
resource.description: The Care Team includes all the people and organizations who plan to participate in the coordination and delivery of care.

property.name: id
property.description: The logical id of the resource, as used in the URL for the resource. Once assigned, this value never changes.

property.name: meta
property.description: The metadata about the resource. This is content that is maintained by the infrastructure. Changes to the content might not always be associated with version changes to the resource.

property.name: implicitRules
property.description: A reference to a set of rules that were followed when the resource was constructed, and which must be understood when processing the content. Often, this is a reference to an implementation guide that defines the special rules along with other profiles etc.

property.name: language
property.description: The base language in which the resource is written.

property.name: text
property.description: A human-readable narrative that contains a summary of the resource and can be used to represent the content of the resource to a human. The narrative need not encode all the structured data, but is required to contain sufficient detail to make it "clinically safe" for a human to just read the narrative. Resource definitions may define what content should be represented in the narrative to ensure clinical safety.

property.name: identifier
property.description: Business identifiers assigned to this care team by the performer or other systems which remain constant as the resource is updated and propagates from server to server.

property.name: status
property.description: Indicates the current state of the care team.

property.name: category
property.description: Identifies what kind of team. This is to support differentiation between multiple co-existing teams, such as care plan team, episode of care team, longitudinal care team.

property.name: name
property.description: A label for human use intended to distinguish like teams. E.g. the "red" vs. "green" trauma teams.

property.name: subject
property.description: Identifies the patient or group whose intended care is handled by the team.

property.name: period
property.description: Indicates when the team did (or is intended to) come into effect and end.

property.name: participant
property.description: Identifies all people and organizations who are expected to be involved in the care team.

property.name: reason
property.description: Describes why the care team exists.

property.name: managingOrganization
property.description: The organization responsible for the care team.

property.name: telecom
property.description: A central contact detail for the care team (that applies to all members).

property.name: note
property.description: Comments made about the CareTeam.

property.name: id
property.description: Unique id for the element within a resource (for internal references). This may be any string value that does not contain spaces.

property.name: role
property.description: Indicates specific responsibility of an individual within the care team, such as "Primary care physician", "Trained social worker counselor", "Caregiver", etc.

property.name: member
property.description: The specific person or organization who is participating/expected to participate in the care team.

property.name: onBehalfOf
property.description: The organization of the practitioner.

property.name: coverage
property.description: When the member is generally available within this care team.

codeset.name: CareTeamStatus
codeset.description: Indicates the status of the care team.

code.name: Proposed
code.description: The care team has been drafted and proposed, but not yet participating in the coordination and delivery of patient care.

code.name: Active
code.description: The care team is currently participating in the coordination and delivery of care.

code.name: Suspended
code.description: The care team is temporarily on hold or suspended and not participating in the coordination and delivery of care.

code.name: Inactive
code.description: The care team was, but is no longer, participating in the coordination and delivery of care.

code.name: EnteredInError
code.description: The care team should have never existed.

resource.name: ChargeItem
resource.description: The resource ChargeItem describes the provision of healthcare provider products for a certain patient, therefore referring not only to the product, but containing in addition details of the provision, like date, time, amounts and participating organizations and persons. Main Usage of the ChargeItem is to enable the billing process and internal cost allocation.

property.name: id
property.description: The logical id of the resource, as used in the URL for the resource. Once assigned, this value never changes.

property.name: meta
property.description: The metadata about the resource. This is content that is maintained by the infrastructure. Changes to the content might not always be associated with version changes to the resource.

property.name: implicitRules
property.description: A reference to a set of rules that were followed when the resource was constructed, and which must be understood when processing the content. Often, this is a reference to an implementation guide that defines the special rules along with other profiles etc.

property.name: language
property.description: The base language in which the resource is written.

property.name: text
property.description: A human-readable narrative that contains a summary of the resource and can be used to represent the content of the resource to a human. The narrative need not encode all the structured data, but is required to contain sufficient detail to make it "clinically safe" for a human to just read the narrative. Resource definitions may define what content should be represented in the narrative to ensure clinical safety.

property.name: identifier
property.description: Identifiers assigned to this event performer or other systems.

property.name: definitionUri
property.description: References the (external) source of pricing information, rules of application for the code this ChargeItem uses.

property.name: definitionCanonical
property.description: References the source of pricing information, rules of application for the code this ChargeItem uses.

property.name: status
property.description: The current state of the ChargeItem.

property.description: ChargeItems can be grouped to larger ChargeItems covering the whole set.

property.description: A code that identifies the charge, like a billing code.

property.description: The individual or set of individuals the action is being or was performed on.

property.description: This ChargeItem has the details of how the associated Encounter should be billed or otherwise be handled by finance systems.

property.name: occurrence
property.description: Date/time(s) or duration when the charged service was applied.

property.name: performer
property.description: Indicates who or what performed or participated in the charged service.

property.name: performingOrganization
property.description: The organization performing the service.

property.name: requestingOrganization
property.description: The organization requesting the service.

property.name: costCenter
property.description: The financial cost center permits the tracking of charge attribution.

property.description: Quantity of which the charge item has been serviced.

property.name: bodysite
property.description: The anatomical location where the related service has been applied.

property.name: unitPriceComponent
property.description: The unit price of the chargable item.

property.name: totalPriceComponent
property.description: The total price for the chargable item, accounting for the quantity.

property.name: overrideReason
property.description: If the list price or the rule-based factor associated with the code is overridden, this attribute can capture a text to indicate the reason for this action.

property.name: enterer
property.description: The device, practitioner, etc. who entered the charge item.

property.name: enteredDate
property.description: Date the charge item was entered.

property.description: Describes why the event occurred in coded or textual form.

property.description: Indicated the rendered service that caused this charge.
