resource.name: DeviceDispense
resource.description: A record of dispensation of a device - i.e., assigning a device to a patient, or to a professional for their use.

property.name: id
property.description: The logical id of the resource, as used in the URL for the resource. Once assigned, this value never changes.

property.name: meta
property.description: The metadata about the resource. This is content that is maintained by the infrastructure. Changes to the content might not always be associated with version changes to the resource.

property.name: implicitRules
property.description: A reference to a set of rules that were followed when the resource was constructed, and which must be understood when processing the content. Often, this is a reference to an implementation guide that defines the special rules along with other profiles etc.

property.name: language
property.description: The base language in which the resource is written.

property.name: text
property.description: A human-readable narrative that contains a summary of the resource and can be used to represent the content of the resource to a human. The narrative need not encode all the structured data, but is required to contain sufficient detail to make it "clinically safe" for a human to just read the narrative. Resource definitions may define what content should be represented in the narrative to ensure clinical safety.

property.name: identifier
property.description: Business identifier for this dispensation.

property.name: basedOn
property.description: The order or request that this dispense is fulfilling.

property.name: partOf
property.description: The bigger event that this dispense is a part of.

property.name: status
property.description: A code specifying the state of the set of dispense events.

property.name: statusReason
property.description: Indicates the reason why a dispense was or was not performed.

property.name: category
property.description: Indicates the type of device dispense.

property.name: device
property.description: Identifies the device being dispensed. This is either a link to a resource representing the details of the device or a simple attribute carrying a code that identifies the device from a known list of devices.

property.name: subject
property.description: A link to a resource representing the person to whom the device is intended.

property.name: receiver
property.description: Identifies the person who picked up the device or the person or location where the device was delivered. This may be a patient or their caregiver, but some cases exist where it can be a healthcare professional or a location.

property.name: encounter
property.description: The encounter that establishes the context for this event.

property.name: supportingInformation
property.description: Additional information that supports the device being dispensed.

property.name: performer
property.description: Indicates who or what performed the event.

property.name: location
property.description: The principal physical location where the dispense was performed.

property.name: type
property.description: Indicates the type of dispensing event that is performed.

property.name: quantity
property.description: The number of devices that have been dispensed.

property.name: preparedDate
property.description: The time when the dispensed product was packaged and reviewed.

property.name: whenHandedOver
property.description: The time the dispensed product was made available to the patient or their representative.

property.name: destination
property.description: Identification of the facility/location where the device was /should be shipped to, as part of the dispense process.

property.name: note
property.description: Extra information about the dispense that could not be conveyed in the other attributes.

property.name: usageInstruction
property.description: The full representation of the instructions.

property.name: eventHistory
property.description: A summary of the events of interest that have occurred, such as when the dispense was verified.

property.name: id
property.description: Unique id for the element within a resource (for internal references). This may be any string value that does not contain spaces.

property.name: function
property.description: Distinguishes the type of performer in the dispense. For example, date enterer, packager, final checker.

property.name: actor
property.description: The device, practitioner, etc. who performed the action. It should be assumed that the actor is the dispenser of the device.

codeset.name: DeviceDispenseStatusCodes
codeset.description: DeviceDispense Status Codes

code.name: Preparation
code.description: The core event has not started yet, but some staging activities have begun (e.g. initial preparing of the device. Preparation stages may be tracked e.g. for planning, supply or billing purposes.

code.name: InProgress
code.description: The dispensed product is ready for pickup.

code.name: Cancelled
code.description: The dispensed product was not and will never be picked up by the patient.

code.name: OnHold
code.description: The dispense process is paused while waiting for an external event to reactivate the dispense. For example, new stock has arrived or the prescriber has called.

code.name: Completed
code.description: The dispensed product has been picked up.

code.name: EnteredInError
code.description: The dispense was entered in error and therefore nullified.

code.name: Stopped
code.description: Actions implied by the dispense have been permanently halted, before all of them occurred.

code.name: Declined
code.description: The dispense was declined and not performed.

code.name: Unknown
code.description: The authoring system does not know which of the status values applies for this dispense. Note: this concept is not to be used for other - one of the listed statuses is presumed to apply, its just now known which one.

resource.name: DeviceMetric
resource.description: Describes a measurement, calculation or setting capability of a device.

property.name: id
property.description: The logical id of the resource, as used in the URL for the resource. Once assigned, this value never changes.

property.name: meta
property.description: The metadata about the resource. This is content that is maintained by the infrastructure. Changes to the content might not always be associated with version changes to the resource.

property.name: implicitRules
property.description: A reference to a set of rules that were followed when the resource was constructed, and which must be understood when processing the content. Often, this is a reference to an implementation guide that defines the special rules along with other profiles etc.

property.name: language
property.description: The base language in which the resource is written.

property.name: text
property.description: A human-readable narrative that contains a summary of the resource and can be used to represent the content of the resource to a human. The narrative need not encode all the structured data, but is required to contain sufficient detail to make it "clinically safe" for a human to just read the narrative. Resource definitions may define what content should be represented in the narrative to ensure clinical safety.

property.name: identifier
property.description: Instance identifiers assigned to a device, by the device or gateway software, manufacturers, other organizations or owners. For example, handle ID.

property.name: type
property.description: Describes the type of the metric. For example: Heart Rate, PEEP Setting, etc.

property.name: unit
property.description: Describes the unit that an observed value determined for this metric will have. For example: Percent, Seconds, etc.

property.name: device
property.description: Describes the link to the Device. This is also known as a channel device.

property.name: operationalStatus
property.description: Indicates current operational state of the device. For example: On, Off, Standby, etc.

property.name: color
property.description: The preferred color associated with the metric (e.g., display color). This is often used to aid clinicians to track and identify parameter types by color. In practice, consider a Patient Monitor that has ECG/HR and Pleth; the metrics are displayed in different characteristic colors, such as HR in blue, BP in green, and PR and SpO2 in magenta.

property.name: category
property.description: Indicates the category of the observation generation process. A DeviceMetric can be for example a setting, measurement, or calculation.

property.name: measurementFrequency
property.description: The frequency at which the metric is taken or recorded. Devices measure metrics at a wide range of frequencies; for example, an ECG might sample measurements in the millisecond range, while an NIBP might trigger only once an hour. Less often, the measurementFrequency may be based on a unit other than time, such as distance (e.g. for a measuring wheel). The update period may be different than the measurement frequency, if the device does not update the published observed value with the same frequency as it was measured.

property.name: calibration
property.description: Describes the calibrations that have been performed or that are required to be performed.

property.name: id
property.description: Unique id for the element within a resource (for internal references). This may be any string value that does not contain spaces.

property.name: type
property.description: Describes the type of the calibration method.

property.name: state
property.description: Describes the state of the calibration.

property.name: time
property.description: Describes the time last calibration has been performed.

codeset.name: DeviceMetricOperationalStatus
codeset.description: Describes the operational status of the DeviceMetric.

code.name: On
code.description: The DeviceMetric is operating and will generate Observations.

code.name: Off
code.description: The DeviceMetric is not operating.

code.name: Standby
code.description: The DeviceMetric is operating, but will not generate any Observations.

code.name: EnteredInError
code.description: The DeviceMetric was entered in error.

codeset.name: ColorCodesOrRGB
codeset.description: This value set includes color codes - either the color names as defined in [CSS4](https://www.w3.org/TR/css-color-4/), or any valid RGB code (```#RRGGBB``` in Hex).

codeset.name: DeviceMetricCategory
codeset.description: Describes the category of the metric.

code.name: Measurement
code.description: Observations generated for this DeviceMetric are measured.

code.name: Setting
code.description: Observations generated for this DeviceMetric is a setting that will influence the behavior of the Device.

code.name: Calculation
code.description: Observations generated for this DeviceMetric are calculated.

code.name: Unspecified
code.description: The category of this DeviceMetric is unspecified.

codeset.name: DeviceMetricCalibrationType
codeset.description: Describes the type of a metric calibration.

code.name: Unspecified
code.description: Metric calibration method has not been identified.

code.name: Offset
code.description: Offset metric calibration method.

code.name: Gain
code.description: Gain metric calibration method.

code.name: TwoPoint
code.description: Two-point metric calibration method.

codeset.name: DeviceMetricCalibrationState
codeset.description: Describes the state of a metric calibration.

code.name: NotCalibrated
code.description: The metric has not been calibrated.

code.name: CalibrationRequired
code.description: The metric needs to be calibrated.

code.name: Calibrated
code.description: The metric has been calibrated.

code.name: Unspecified
code.description: The state of calibration of this metric is unspecified.

resource.name: DeviceRequest
resource.description: Represents a request for a patient to employ a medical device. The device may be an implantable device, or an external assistive device, such as a walker.

property.name: id
property.description: The logical id of the resource, as used in the URL for the resource. Once assigned, this value never changes.

property.name: meta
property.description: The metadata about the resource. This is content that is maintained by the infrastructure. Changes to the content might not always be associated with version changes to the resource.

property.name: implicitRules
property.description: A reference to a set of rules that were followed when the resource was constructed, and which must be understood when processing the content. Often, this is a reference to an implementation guide that defines the special rules along with other profiles etc.

property.name: language
property.description: The base language in which the resource is written.

property.name: text
property.description: A human-readable narrative that contains a summary of the resource and can be used to represent the content of the resource to a human. The narrative need not encode all the structured data, but is required to contain sufficient detail to make it "clinically safe" for a human to just read the narrative. Resource definitions may define what content should be represented in the narrative to ensure clinical safety.

property.name: identifier
property.description: Identifiers assigned to this order by the orderer or by the receiver.

property.name: instantiatesCanonical
property.description: The URL pointing to a FHIR-defined protocol, guideline, orderset or other definition that is adhered to in whole or in part by this DeviceRequest.

property.name: instantiatesUri
property.description: The URL pointing to an externally maintained protocol, guideline, orderset or other definition that is adhered to in whole or in part by this DeviceRequest.

property.name: basedOn
property.description: Plan/proposal/order fulfilled by this request.

property.name: replaces
property.description: The request takes the place of the referenced completed or terminated request(s).

property.name: groupIdentifier
property.description: A shared identifier common to multiple independent Request instances that were activated/authorized more or less simultaneously by a single author. The presence of the same identifier on each request ties those requests together and may have business ramifications in terms of reporting of results, billing, etc. E.g. a requisition number shared by a set of lab tests ordered together, or a prescription number shared by all meds ordered at one time.

property.name: status
property.description: The status of the request.

property.name: intent
property.description: Whether the request is a proposal, plan, an original order or a reflex order.

property.name: priority
property.description: Indicates how quickly the request should be addressed with respect to other requests.

property.name: doNotPerform
property.description: If true, indicates that the provider is asking for the patient to either stop using or to not start using the specified device or category of devices. For example, the patient has undergone surgery and the provider is indicating that the patient should not wear contact lenses.

property.name: code
property.description: The details of the device to be used.

property.name: quantity
property.description: The number of devices to be provided.

property.name: parameter
property.description: Specific parameters for the ordered item. For example, the prism value for lenses.

property.name: subject
property.description: The patient who will use the device.

property.name: encounter
property.description: An encounter that provides additional context in which this request is made.

property.name: occurrence
property.description: The timing schedule for the use of the device. The Schedule data type allows many different expressions, for example. "Every 8 hours"; "Three times a day"; "1/2 an hour before breakfast for 10 days from 23-Dec 2011:"; "15 Oct 2013, 17 Oct 2013 and 1 Nov 2013".

property.name: authoredOn
property.description: When the request transitioned to being actionable.

property.name: requester
property.description: The individual or entity who initiated the request and has responsibility for its activation.

property.name: performer
property.description: The desired individual or entity to provide the device to the subject of the request (e.g., patient, location).

property.name: reason
property.description: Reason or justification for the use of this device.

property.name: asNeeded
property.description: This status is to indicate whether the request is a PRN or may be given as needed.

property.name: asNeededFor
property.description: The reason for using the device.

property.name: insurance
property.description: Insurance plans, coverage extensions, pre-authorizations and/or pre-determinations that may be required for delivering the requested service.

property.name: supportingInfo
property.description: Additional clinical information about the patient that may influence the request fulfilment. For example, this may include where on the subjects body the device will be used (i.e. the target site).

property.name: note
property.description: Details about this request that were not represented at all or sufficiently in one of the attributes provided in a class. These may include for example a comment, an instruction, or a note associated with the statement.

property.name: relevantHistory
property.description: Key events in the history of the request.

property.name: id
property.description: Unique id for the element within a resource (for internal references). This may be any string value that does not contain spaces.

property.name: code
property.description: A code or string that identifies the device detail being asserted.

property.name: value
property.description: The value of the device detail.

resource.name: DeviceUsage
resource.description: A record of a device being used by a patient where the record is the result of a report from the patient or a clinician.

property.name: id
property.description: The logical id of the resource, as used in the URL for the resource. Once assigned, this value never changes.

property.name: meta
property.description: The metadata about the resource. This is content that is maintained by the infrastructure. Changes to the content might not always be associated with version changes to the resource.

property.name: implicitRules
property.description: A reference to a set of rules that were followed when the resource was constructed, and which must be understood when processing the content. Often, this is a reference to an implementation guide that defines the special rules along with other profiles etc.

property.name: language
property.description: The base language in which the resource is written.

property.name: text
property.description: A human-readable narrative that contains a summary of the resource and can be used to represent the content of the resource to a human. The narrative need not encode all the structured data, but is required to contain sufficient detail to make it "clinically safe" for a human to just read the narrative. Resource definitions may define what content should be represented in the narrative to ensure clinical safety.

property.name: identifier
property.description: An external identifier for this statement such as an IRI.

property.name: basedOn
property.description: A plan, proposal or order that is fulfilled in whole or in part by this DeviceUsage.

property.name: status
property.description: A code representing the patient or other sources judgment about the state of the device used that this statement is about. Generally this will be active or completed.

property.name: category
property.description: This attribute indicates a category for the statement - The device statement may be made in an inpatient or outpatient settting (inpatient | outpatient | community | patientspecified).

property.name: patient
property.description: The patient who used the device.

property.name: derivedFrom
property.description: Allows linking the DeviceUsage to the underlying Request, or to other information that supports or is used to derive the DeviceUsage.

property.name: context
property.description: The encounter or episode of care that establishes the context for this device use statement.

property.name: timing
property.description: How often the device was used.

property.name: dateAsserted
property.description: The time at which the statement was recorded by informationSource.

property.name: usageStatus
property.description: The status of the device usage, for example always, sometimes, never. This is not the same as the status of the statement.

property.name: usageReason
property.description: The reason for asserting the usage status - for example forgot, lost, stolen, broken.

property.name: adherence
property.description: This indicates how or if the device is being used.

property.name: informationSource
property.description: Who reported the device was being used by the patient.

property.name: device
property.description: Code or Reference to device used.

property.name: reason
property.description: Reason or justification for the use of the device. A coded concept, or another resource whose existence justifies this DeviceUsage.

property.name: bodySite
property.description: Indicates the anotomic location on the subjects body where the device was used ( i.e. the target).

property.name: note
property.description: Details about the device statement that were not represented at all or sufficiently in one of the attributes provided in a class. These may include for example a comment, an instruction, or a note associated with the statement.

property.name: id
property.description: Unique id for the element within a resource (for internal references). This may be any string value that does not contain spaces.

property.name: code
property.description: Type of adherence.

property.name: reason
property.description: Reason for adherence type.

codeset.name: DeviceUsageStatus
codeset.description: A coded concept indicating the current status of the Device Usage.

code.name: Active
code.description: The device is still being used.

code.name: Completed
code.description: The device is no longer being used.

code.name: NotDone
code.description: The device was not used.

code.name: EnteredInError
code.description: The statement was recorded incorrectly.

code.name: Intended
code.description: The device may be used at some time in the future.

code.name: Stopped
code.description: Actions implied by the statement have been permanently halted, before all of them occurred.

code.name: OnHold
code.description: Actions implied by the statement have been temporarily halted, but are expected to continue later. May also be called "suspended".

resource.name: DiagnosticReport
resource.description: The findings and interpretation of diagnostic tests performed on patients, groups of patients, products, substances, devices, and locations, and/or specimens derived from these. The report includes clinical context such as requesting provider information, and some mix of atomic results, images, textual and coded interpretations, and formatted representation of diagnostic reports. The report also includes non-clinical context such as batch analysis and stability reporting of products and substances.

property.name: id
property.description: The logical id of the resource, as used in the URL for the resource. Once assigned, this value never changes.

property.name: meta
property.description: The metadata about the resource. This is content that is maintained by the infrastructure. Changes to the content might not always be associated with version changes to the resource.

property.name: implicitRules
property.description: A reference to a set of rules that were followed when the resource was constructed, and which must be understood when processing the content. Often, this is a reference to an implementation guide that defines the special rules along with other profiles etc.

property.name: language
property.description: The base language in which the resource is written.

property.name: text
property.description: A human-readable narrative that contains a summary of the resource and can be used to represent the content of the resource to a human. The narrative need not encode all the structured data, but is required to contain sufficient detail to make it "clinically safe" for a human to just read the narrative. Resource definitions may define what content should be represented in the narrative to ensure clinical safety.

property.name: identifier
property.description: Identifiers assigned to this report by the performer or other systems.

property.name: basedOn
property.description: Details concerning a service requested.

property.name: status
property.description: The status of the diagnostic report.

property.name: category
property.description: A code that classifies the clinical discipline, department or diagnostic service that created the report (e.g. cardiology, biochemistry, hematology, MRI). This is used for searching, sorting and display purposes.

property.name: code
property.description: A code or name that describes this diagnostic report.

property.name: subject
property.description: The subject of the report. Usually, but not always, this is a patient. However, diagnostic services also perform analyses on specimens collected from a variety of other sources.

property.name: encounter
property.description: The healthcare event (e.g. a patient and healthcare provider interaction) which this DiagnosticReport is about.

property.name: effective
property.description: The time or time-period the observed values are related to. When the subject of the report is a patient, this is usually either the time of the procedure or of specimen collection(s), but very often the source of the date/time is not known, only the date/time itself.

property.name: issued
property.description: The date and time that this version of the report was made available to providers, typically after the report was reviewed and verified.

property.name: performer
property.description: The diagnostic service that is responsible for issuing the report.

property.name: resultsInterpreter
property.description: The practitioner or organization that is responsible for the reports conclusions and interpretations.

property.name: specimen
property.description: Details about the specimens on which this diagnostic report is based.

property.name: result
property.description: [Observations](observation.html) that are part of this diagnostic report.

property.name: note
property.description: Comments about the diagnostic report.

property.name: study
property.description: One or more links to full details of any study performed during the diagnostic investigation. An ImagingStudy might comprise a set of radiologic images obtained via a procedure that are analyzed as a group. Typically, this is imaging performed by DICOM enabled modalities, but this is not required. A fully enabled PACS viewer can use this information to provide views of the source images. A GenomicStudy might comprise one or more analyses, each serving a specific purpose. These analyses may vary in method (e.g., karyotyping, CNV, or SNV detection), performer, software, devices used, or regions targeted.

property.name: supportingInfo
property.description: This backbone element contains supporting information that was used in the creation of the report not included in the results already included in the report.

property.name: media
property.description: A list of key images or data associated with this report. The images or data are generally created during the diagnostic process, and may be directly of the patient, or of treated specimens (i.e. slides of interest).

property.name: composition
property.description: Reference to a Composition resource instance that provides structure for organizing the contents of the DiagnosticReport.

property.name: conclusion
property.description: Concise and clinically contextualized summary conclusion (interpretation/impression) of the diagnostic report.

property.name: conclusionCode
property.description: One or more codes that represent the summary conclusion (interpretation/impression) of the diagnostic report.

property.name: presentedForm
property.description: Rich text representation of the entire result as issued by the diagnostic service. Multiple formats are allowed but they SHALL be semantically equivalent.

property.name: id
property.description: Unique id for the element within a resource (for internal references). This may be any string value that does not contain spaces.

property.name: type
property.description: The code value for the role of the supporting information in the diagnostic report.

property.name: reference
property.description: The reference for the supporting information in the diagnostic report.

property.name: id
property.description: Unique id for the element within a resource (for internal references). This may be any string value that does not contain spaces.

property.name: comment
property.description: A comment about the image or data. Typically, this is used to provide an explanation for why the image or data is included, or to draw the viewers attention to important features.

property.name: link
property.description: Reference to the image or data source.

codeset.name: DiagnosticReportStatus
codeset.description: The status of the diagnostic report.

code.name: Registered
code.description: The existence of the report is registered, but there is nothing yet available.

code.name: Partial
code.description: This is a partial (e.g. initial, interim or preliminary) report: data in the report may be incomplete or unverified.

code.name: Preliminary
code.description: Verified early results are available, but not all results are final.

code.name: Modified
code.description: Prior to being final, the report has been modified. This includes any change in the results, diagnosis, narrative text, or other content of a non-finalized (e.g., preliminary) report that has been issued.

code.name: Final
code.description: The report is complete and verified by an authorized person.

code.name: Amended
code.description: Subsequent to being final, the report has been modified. This includes any change in the results, diagnosis, narrative text, or other content of a report that has been issued.

code.name: Corrected
code.description: Subsequent to being final, the report has been modified to correct an error in the report or referenced results.

code.name: Appended
code.description: Subsequent to being final, the report has been modified by adding new content. The existing content is unchanged.

code.name: Cancelled
code.description: The report is unavailable because the measurement was not started or not completed (also sometimes called "aborted").

code.name: EnteredInError
code.description: The report has been withdrawn following a previous final release. This electronic record should never have existed, though it is possible that real-world decisions were based on it. (If real-world activity has occurred, the status should be "cancelled" rather than "entered-in-error".).

code.name: Unknown
code.description: The authoring/source system does not know which of the status values currently applies for this observation. Note: This concept is not to be used for "other" - one of the listed statuses is presumed to apply, but the authoring/source system does not know which.

resource.name: DocumentReference
resource.description: A reference to a document of any kind for any purpose. While the term document implies a more narrow focus, for this resource this "document" encompasses *any* serialized object with a mime-type, it includes formal patient-centric documents (CDA), clinical notes, scanned paper, non-patient specific documents like policy text, as well as a photo, video, or audio recording acquired or used in healthcare. The DocumentReference resource provides metadata about the document so that the document can be discovered and managed. The actual content may be inline base64 encoded data or provided by direct reference.

property.name: id
property.description: The logical id of the resource, as used in the URL for the resource. Once assigned, this value never changes.

property.name: meta
property.description: The metadata about the resource. This is content that is maintained by the infrastructure. Changes to the content might not always be associated with version changes to the resource.

property.name: implicitRules
property.description: A reference to a set of rules that were followed when the resource was constructed, and which must be understood when processing the content. Often, this is a reference to an implementation guide that defines the special rules along with other profiles etc.

property.name: language
property.description: The base language in which the resource is written.

property.name: text
property.description: A human-readable narrative that contains a summary of the resource and can be used to represent the content of the resource to a human. The narrative need not encode all the structured data, but is required to contain sufficient detail to make it "clinically safe" for a human to just read the narrative. Resource definitions may define what content should be represented in the narrative to ensure clinical safety.

property.name: identifier
property.description: Other business identifiers associated with the document, including version independent identifiers.

property.name: version
property.description: An explicitly assigned identifer of a variation of the content in the DocumentReference.

property.name: basedOn
property.description: A procedure that is fulfilled in whole or in part by the creation of this media.

property.name: status
property.description: The status of this document reference.

property.name: docStatus
property.description: The status of the underlying document.

property.name: modality
property.description: Imaging modality used. This may include both acquisition and non-acquisition modalities.

property.name: type
property.description: Specifies the particular kind of document referenced (e.g. History and Physical, Discharge Summary, Progress Note). This usually equates to the purpose of making the document referenced.

property.name: category
property.description: A categorization for the type of document referenced - helps for indexing and searching. This may be implied by or derived from the code specified in the DocumentReference.type.

property.name: subject
property.description: Who or what the document is about. The document can be about a person, (patient or healthcare practitioner), a device (e.g. a machine) or even a group of subjects (such as a document about a herd of farm animals, or a set of patients that share a common exposure).

property.name: context
property.description: Describes the clinical encounter or type of care that the document content is associated with.

property.name: event
property.description: This list of codes represents the main clinical acts, such as a colonoscopy or an appendectomy, being documented. In some cases, the event is inherent in the type Code, such as a "History and Physical Report" in which the procedure being documented is necessarily a "History and Physical" act.

property.name: bodySite
property.description: The anatomic structures included in the document.

property.name: facilityType
property.description: The kind of facility where the patient was seen.

property.name: practiceSetting
property.description: This property may convey specifics about the practice setting where the content was created, often reflecting the clinical specialty.

property.name: period
property.description: The time period over which the service that is described by the document was provided.

property.name: date
property.description: When the document reference was created.

property.name: author
property.description: Identifies who is responsible for adding the information to the document.

property.name: attester
property.description: A participant who has authenticated the accuracy of the document.

property.name: custodian
property.description: Identifies the organization or group who is responsible for ongoing maintenance of and access to the document.

property.name: relatesTo
property.description: Relationships that this document has with other document references that already exist.

property.name: description
property.description: Human-readable description of the source document.

property.name: securityLabel
property.description: A set of Security-Tag codes specifying the level of privacy/security of the Document found at DocumentReference.content.attachment.url. Note that DocumentReference.meta.security contains the security labels of the data elements in DocumentReference, while DocumentReference.securityLabel contains the security labels for the document the reference refers to. The distinction recognizes that the document may contain sensitive information, while the DocumentReference is metadata about the document and thus might not be as sensitive as the document. For example: a psychotherapy episode may contain highly sensitive information, while the metadata may simply indicate that some episode happened.

property.name: content
property.description: The document and format referenced. If there are multiple content element repetitions, these must all represent the same document in different format, or attachment metadata.

property.name: id
property.description: Unique id for the element within a resource (for internal references). This may be any string value that does not contain spaces.

property.name: mode
property.description: The type of attestation the authenticator offers.

property.name: time
property.description: When the document was attested by the party.

property.name: party
property.description: Who attested the document in the specified way.

property.name: id
property.description: Unique id for the element within a resource (for internal references). This may be any string value that does not contain spaces.

property.name: code
property.description: The type of relationship that this document has with anther document.

property.name: target
property.description: The target document of this relationship.

property.name: id
property.description: Unique id for the element within a resource (for internal references). This may be any string value that does not contain spaces.

property.name: attachment
property.description: The document or URL of the document along with critical metadata to prove content has integrity.

property.name: profile
property.description: An identifier of the document constraints, encoding, structure, and template that the document conforms to beyond the base format indicated in the mimeType.

property.name: id
property.description: Unique id for the element within a resource (for internal references). This may be any string value that does not contain spaces.

property.name: value
property.description: Code|uri|canonical.

operation.name: docref
operation.description: This operation is used to return all the references to documents related to a patient. The operation requires a patient id and takes the optional input parameters: - start date - end date - document type and returns a [Bundle](bundle.html) of type "searchset" containing [DocumentReference](documentreference.html) resources for the patient. If the server has or can create documents that are related to the patient, and that are available for the given user, the server returns the DocumentReference resources needed to support the records. The principle intended use for this operation is to provide a provider or patient with access to their available document information. This operation is *different* from a search by patient and type and date range because: 1. It is used to request a server to *generate* a document based on the specified parameters. 1. If no parameters are specified, the server SHALL return a DocumentReference to the patient's most current CCD 1. If the server cannot *generate* a document based on the specified parameters, the operation will return an empty search bundle. This operation is the *same* as a FHIR RESTful search by patient, type and date range because: 1. References for *existing* documents that meet the requirements of the request SHOULD also be returned unless the client indicates they are only interested in 'on-demand' documents using the *on-demand* parameter.

parameter.name: patient
parameter.description: The id of the patient resource located on the server on which this operation is executed. If there is no match, an empty Bundle is returned

parameter.name: start
parameter.description: The date range relates to care dates, not record currency dates - e.g. all records relating to care provided in a certain date range. If no start date is provided, all documents prior to the end date are in scope. If neither a start date nor an end date is provided, the most recent or current document is in scope. The client **SHOULD** provide values precise to the second + time offset.

parameter.name: end
parameter.description: The date range relates to care dates, not record currency dates - e.g. all records relating to care provided in a certain date range. If no end date is provided, all documents subsequent to the start date are in scope. If neither a start date nor an end date is provided, the most recent or current document is in scope. The client **SHOULD** provide values precise to the second + time offset.

parameter.name: type
parameter.description: The type relates to document type e.g. for the LOINC code for a C-CDA Clinical Summary of Care (CCD) is 34133-9 (Summary of episode note). If no type is provided, the CCD document, if available, SHALL be in scope and all other document types MAY be in scope

parameter.name: on-demand
parameter.description: This on-demand parameter allows client to dictate whether they are requesting only on-demand or both on-demand and stable documents (or delayed/deferred assembly) that meet the query parameters

parameter.name: return
parameter.description: The bundle type is "searchset"containing [DocumentReference](documentreference.html) resources.

operation.name: generate
operation.description: A client can ask a server to generate a document reference from a document.The server reads the existing document and generates a matching DocumentReferenceresource, or returns one it has previously generated. Servers may be able to return or generate document references for the following types of content:

parameter.name: url
parameter.description: The URL to the source document. This may be a general URL or a Binary or a Composition or a Bundle.

parameter.name: persist
parameter.description: Whether to store the document at the document end-point (/Document) or not, once it is generated (default is for the server to decide).

parameter.name: return
parameter.description: The bundle type is "searchset"containing [DocumentReference](documentreference.html) resource and may include a Binary. If the input url refers to another server, it is at the discretion of the server whether to retrieve it or return an error.

resource.name: Encounter
resource.description: An interaction between a patient and healthcare provider(s) for the purpose of providing healthcare service(s) or assessing the health status of a patient. Encounter is primarily used to record information about the actual activities that occurred, where Appointment is used to record planned activities.

property.name: id
property.description: The logical id of the resource, as used in the URL for the resource. Once assigned, this value never changes.

property.name: meta
property.description: The metadata about the resource. This is content that is maintained by the infrastructure. Changes to the content might not always be associated with version changes to the resource.

property.name: implicitRules
property.description: A reference to a set of rules that were followed when the resource was constructed, and which must be understood when processing the content. Often, this is a reference to an implementation guide that defines the special rules along with other profiles etc.

property.name: language
property.description: The base language in which the resource is written.

property.name: text
property.description: A human-readable narrative that contains a summary of the resource and can be used to represent the content of the resource to a human. The narrative need not encode all the structured data, but is required to contain sufficient detail to make it "clinically safe" for a human to just read the narrative. Resource definitions may define what content should be represented in the narrative to ensure clinical safety.

property.name: identifier
property.description: Identifier(s) by which this encounter is known.

property.name: status
property.description: The current state of the encounter (not the state of the patient within the encounter - that is subjectState).

property.name: class
property.description: Concepts representing classification of patient encounter such as ambulatory (outpatient), inpatient, emergency, home health or others due to local variations.

property.name: priority
property.description: Indicates the urgency of the encounter.

property.name: type
property.description: Specific type of encounter (e.g. e-mail consultation, surgical day-care, skilled nursing, rehabilitation).

property.name: serviceType
property.description: Broad categorization of the service that is to be provided (e.g. cardiology).

property.name: subject
property.description: The patient or group related to this encounter. In some use-cases the patient MAY not be present, such as a case meeting about a patient between several practitioners or a careteam.

property.name: subjectStatus
property.description: The subjectStatus value can be used to track the patients status within the encounter. It details whether the patient has arrived or departed, has been triaged or is currently in a waiting status.

property.name: episodeOfCare
property.description: Where a specific encounter should be classified as a part of a specific episode(s) of care this field should be used. This association can facilitate grouping of related encounters together for a specific purpose, such as government reporting, issue tracking, association via a common problem. The association is recorded on the encounter as these are typically created after the episode of care and grouped on entry rather than editing the episode of care to append another encounter to it (the episode of care could span years).

property.name: basedOn
property.description: The request this encounter satisfies (e.g. incoming referral or procedure request).

property.name: careTeam
property.description: The group(s) of individuals, organizations that are allocated to participate in this encounter. The participants backbone will record the actuals of when these individuals participated during the encounter.

property.name: partOf
property.description: Another Encounter of which this encounter is a part of (administratively or in time).

property.name: serviceProvider
property.description: The organization that is primarily responsible for this Encounters services. This MAY be the same as the organization on the Patient record, however it could be different, such as if the actor performing the services was from an external organization (which may be billed seperately) for an external consultation. Refer to the colonoscopy example on the Encounter examples tab.

property.name: participant
property.description: The list of people responsible for providing the service.

property.name: appointment
property.description: The appointment that scheduled this encounter.

property.name: virtualService
property.description: Connection details of a virtual service (e.g. conference call).

property.name: actualPeriod
property.description: The actual start and end time of the encounter.

property.name: plannedStartDate
property.description: The planned start date/time (or admission date) of the encounter.

property.name: plannedEndDate
property.description: The planned end date/time (or discharge date) of the encounter.

property.name: length
property.description: Actual quantity of time the encounter lasted. This excludes the time during leaves of absence.When missing it is the time in between the start and end values.

property.name: reason
property.description: The list of medical reasons that are expected to be addressed during the episode of care.

property.name: diagnosis
property.description: The list of diagnosis relevant to this encounter.

property.name: account
property.description: The set of accounts that may be used for billing for this Encounter.

property.name: dietPreference
property.description: Diet preferences reported by the patient.

property.name: specialArrangement
property.description: Any special requests that have been made for this encounter, such as the provision of specific equipment or other things.

property.name: specialCourtesy
property.description: Special courtesies that may be provided to the patient during the encounter (VIP, board member, professional courtesy).

property.name: admission
property.description: Details about the stay during which a healthcare service is provided.This does not describe the event of admitting the patient, but rather any information that is relevant from the time of admittance until the time of discharge.

property.name: location
property.description: List of locations where the patient has been during this encounter.

property.name: id
property.description: Unique id for the element within a resource (for internal references). This may be any string value that does not contain spaces.

property.name: type
property.description: Role of participant in encounter.

property.name: period
property.description: The period of time that the specified participant participated in the encounter. These can overlap or be sub-sets of the overall encounters period.

property.name: actor
property.description: Person involved in the encounter, the patient/group is also included here to indicate that the patient was actually participating in the encounter. Not including the patient here covers use cases such as a case meeting between practitioners about a patient - non contact times.

property.name: id
property.description: Unique id for the element within a resource (for internal references). This may be any string value that does not contain spaces.

property.name: use
property.description: What the reason value should be used as e.g. Chief Complaint, Health Concern, Health Maintenance (including screening).

property.name: value
property.description: Reason the encounter takes place, expressed as a code or a reference to another resource. For admissions, this can be used for a coded admission diagnosis.

property.name: id
property.description: Unique id for the element within a resource (for internal references). This may be any string value that does not contain spaces.

property.name: condition
property.description: The coded diagnosis or a reference to a Condition (with other resources referenced in the evidence.detail), the use property will indicate the purpose of this specific diagnosis.

property.name: use
property.description: Role that this diagnosis has within the encounter (e.g. admission, billing, discharge ).

property.name: id
property.description: Unique id for the element within a resource (for internal references). This may be any string value that does not contain spaces.

property.name: preAdmissionIdentifier
property.description: Pre-admission identifier.

property.name: origin
property.description: The location/organization from which the patient came before admission.

property.name: admitSource
property.description: From where patient was admitted (physician referral, transfer).

property.name: reAdmission
property.description: Indicates that this encounter is directly related to a prior admission, often because the conditions addressed in the prior admission were not fully addressed.

property.name: destination
property.description: Location/organization to which the patient is discharged.

property.name: dischargeDisposition
property.description: Category or kind of location after discharge.

property.name: id
property.description: Unique id for the element within a resource (for internal references). This may be any string value that does not contain spaces.

property.name: location
property.description: The location where the encounter takes place.

property.name: status
property.description: The status of the participants presence at the specified location during the period specified. If the participant is no longer at the location, then the period will have an end date/time.

property.name: form
property.description: This will be used to specify the required levels (bed/ward/room/etc.) desired to be recorded to simplify either messaging or query.

property.name: period
property.description: Time period during which the patient was present at the location.

codeset.name: EncounterLocationStatus
codeset.description: The status of the location.

code.name: Planned
code.description: The patient is planned to be moved to this location at some point in the future.

code.name: Active
code.description: The patient is currently at this location, or was between the period specified.A system may update these records when the patient leaves the location to either reserved, or completed.

code.name: Reserved
code.description: This location is held empty for this patient.

code.name: Completed
code.description: The patient was at this location during the period specified.Not to be used when the patient is currently at the location.

operation.name: everything
operation.description: This operation is used to return all the information related to an encounter described in the resource on which this operation is invoked. The response is a bundle of type "searchset". At a minimum, the encounter resource itself is returned, along with any other resources that the server has available for the given encounter for the user. The server also returns whatever resources are needed to support the records - e.g. linked practitioners, locations, organizations etc. The principle intended use for this operation is to provide a patient with access to their record, or to allow a client to retrieve everything for an encounter for efficient display).The server SHOULD return all resources it has that:* are included in the encounter compartment for the identified encounter (have a reference to the encounter)* are referenced by the standard extenstion for associating an encounter (where no reference element exists) http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/encounter-associatedEncounter* the server believes are relevant to the context of the encounter for any other reason (internally defined/decided)* any resource referenced by the above, including binaries and attachments (to make a more complete package)In the US Realm, at a mimimum, the resources returned SHALL include all the data covered by the meaningful use common data elements (see [DAF](http://hl7.org/fhir/us/daf) for further guidance). Other applicable implementation guides may make additional rules about the information that is returned. Note that for many resources, the exact nature of the link to encounter can be ambiguous (e.g. for a DiagnosticReport, is it the encounter when it was initiated, or when it was reported?)

parameter.name: _since
parameter.description: Resources updated after this period will be included in the response. The intent of this parameter is to allow a client to request only records that have changed since the last request, based on either the return header time, or or (for asynchronous use), the transaction time

parameter.name: _type
parameter.description: One or more parameters, each containing one or more comma-delimited FHIR resource types to include in the return resources. In the absense of any specified types, the server returns all resource types

parameter.name: _count
parameter.description: See discussion below on the utility of paging through the results of the $everything operation

parameter.name: return
parameter.description: The bundle type is "searchset"

resource.name: EncounterHistory

property.name: encounter

property.name: identifier

property.name: status

property.name: serviceType

property.name: subject

property.name: subjectStatus

property.name: actualPeriod

property.name: plannedStartDate
property.description: The planned start date/time (or admission date) of the encounter.

property.name: plannedEndDate

property.name: length

code.name: Waitlist
code.description: This episode has been placed on a waitlist, pending the episode being made active (or cancelled).

code.name: Active

code.name: Onhold

code.name: Finished

code.name: Cancelled

It indicates that services terminated outside the planned/expected workflow.

code.name: EnteredInError

operation.name: everything
operation.description: This operation is used to return all the information related to an episodeofcare described in the resource on which this operation is invoked. The response is a bundle of type "searchset". At a minimum, the episodeofcare resource itself is returned, along with any other resources that the server has available for the given episodeofcare for the user. The server also returns whatever resources are needed to support the records - e.g. linked practitioners, locations, organizations etc. The principle intended use for this operation is to provide a patient with access to their record, or to allow a client to retrieve everything for an episodeofcare for efficient display).The server SHOULD return all resources it has that:* are included in the episodeofcare compartment for the identified episodeofcare (have a reference to the episodeofcare)* are referenced by the standard extension for associating an episodeofcare (where no reference element exists) http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/workflow-episodeOfCare* the server believes are relevant to the context of the episodeofcare for any other reason (internally defined/decided)* any resource referenced by the above, including binaries and attachments (to make a more complete package)

parameter.name: _type
parameter.description: One or more parameters, each containing one or more comma-delimited FHIR resource types to include in the return resources. In the absense of any specified types, the server returns all resource types

parameter.name: _count
parameter.description: See discussion below on the utility of paging through the results of the $everything operation

parameter.name: return
parameter.description: The bundle type is "searchset"

property.description: The status of the resource instance.

property.name: type
property.description: The category of claim, e.g. oral, pharmacy, vision, institutional, professional.

property.name: subType
property.description: A finer grained suite of claim type codes which may convey additional information such as Inpatient vs Outpatient and/or a specialty service.

property.name: use
property.description: A code to indicate whether the nature of the request is: Claim - A request to an Insurer to adjudicate the supplied charges for health care goods and services under the identified policy and to pay the determined Benefit amount, if any; Preauthorization - A request to an Insurer to adjudicate the supplied proposed future charges for health care goods and services under the identified policy and to approve the services and provide the expected benefit amounts and potentially to reserve funds to pay the benefits when Claims for the indicated services are later submitted; or, Pre-determination - A request to an Insurer to adjudicate the supplied what if charges for health care goods and services under the identified policy and report back what the Benefit payable would be had the services actually been provided.

property.name: patient
property.description: The party to whom the professional services and/or products have been supplied or are being considered and for whom actual for forecast reimbursement is sought.

property.name: billablePeriod
property.description: The period for which charges are being submitted.

property.name: created
property.description: The date this resource was created.

property.name: enterer
property.description: Individual who created the claim, predetermination or preauthorization.

property.name: insurer
property.description: The party responsible for authorization, adjudication and reimbursement.

property.name: provider
property.description: The provider which is responsible for the claim, predetermination or preauthorization.

property.name: priority
property.description: The provider-required urgency of processing the request. Typical values include: stat, normal deferred.

property.name: fundsReserveRequested
property.description: A code to indicate whether and for whom funds are to be reserved for future claims.

property.name: fundsReserve
property.description: A code, used only on a response to a preauthorization, to indicate whether the benefits payable have been reserved and for whom.

property.name: related
property.description: Other claims which are related to this claim such as prior submissions or claims for related services or for the same event.

property.name: prescription
property.description: Prescription is the document/authorization given to the claim author for them to provide products and services for which consideration (reimbursement) is sought. Could be a RX for medications, an order for oxygen or wheelchair or physiotherapy treatments.

property.name: originalPrescription
property.description: Original prescription which has been superseded by this prescription to support the dispensing of pharmacy services, medications or products.

property.name: event
property.description: Information code for an event with a corresponding date or period.

property.name: payee
property.description: The party to be reimbursed for cost of the products and services according to the terms of the policy.

property.name: referral
property.description: The referral information received by the claim author, it is not to be used when the author generates a referral for a patient. A copy of that referral may be provided as supporting information. Some insurers require proof of referral to pay for services or to pay specialist rates for services.

property.name: encounter
property.description: Healthcare encounters related to this claim.

property.name: facility

property.name: outcome

property.description: An area where general notes can be placed about this specific procedure.

This electronic record should never have existed, though it is possible that real-world decisions were based on it. (If real-world activity has occurred, the status should be "cancelled" rather than "entered-in-error".).

resource.description: Describes the intended objective(s) for a patient, group or organization care, for example, weight loss, restoring an activity of daily living, obtaining herd immunity via immunization, meeting a process improvement objective, etc.

property.name: id
property.description: The logical id of the resource, as used in the URL for the resource. Once assigned, this value never changes.

property.name: meta
property.description: The metadata about the resource. This is content that is maintained by the infrastructure. Changes to the content might not always be associated with version changes to the resource.

Resource definitions may define what content should be represented in the narrative to ensure clinical safety.

property.description: Business identifiers assigned to this goal by the performer or other systems which remain constant as the resource is updated and propagates from server to server.

property.name: achievementStatus
property.description: Describes the progression, or lack thereof, towards the goal against the target.

property.name: category
property.description: Indicates a category the goal falls within.

property.name: continuous
property.description: After meeting the goal, ongoing activity is needed to sustain the goal objective.

property.name: priority
property.description: Identifies the mutually agreed level of importance associated with reaching/sustaining the goal.

property.name: description
property.description: Human-readable and/or coded description of a specific desired objective of care, such as "control blood pressure" or "negotiate an obstacle course" or "dance with child at wedding".

property.name: subject
property.description: Identifies the patient, group or organization for whom the goal is being established.

property.name: start
property.description: The date or event after which the goal should begin being pursued.

property.name: target
property.description: Indicates what should be done by when.

property.name: statusDate
property.description: Identifies when the current status. I.e. When initially created, when achieved, when cancelled, etc.

property.name: statusReason
property.description: Captures the reason for the current status.

property.name: source
property.description: Indicates whose goal this is - patient goal, practitioner goal, etc.

property.name: addresses
property.description: The identified conditions and other health record elements that are intended to be addressed by the goal.

property.name: note
property.description: Any comments related to the goal.

property.name: outcome
property.description: Identifies the change (or lack of change) at the point when the status of the goal is assessed.

property.description: Unique id for the element within a resource (for internal references). This may be any string value that does not contain spaces.

property.name: measure
property.description: The parameter whose value is being tracked, e.g. body weight, blood pressure, or hemoglobin A1c level.

property.name: detail
property.description: The target value of the focus to be achieved to signify the fulfillment of the goal, e.g. 150 pounds, 7.0%. Either the high or low or both values of the range can be specified. When a low value is missing, it indicates that the goal is achieved at any focus value at or below the high value. Similarly, if the high value is missing, it indicates that the goal is achieved at any focus value at or above the low value.

property.name: due
property.description: Indicates either the date or the duration after start by which the goal should be met.

code.name: Planned

code.name: Accepted

code.description: The goal remains a long term objective but is no longer being actively pursued for a temporary period of time.

code.name: Completed
code.description: The goal is no longer being sought.

code.name: Cancelled
code.description: The goal has been abandoned.

code.name: EnteredInError
code.description: The goal was entered in error and voided.

code.name: Rejected
code.description: A proposed goal was rejected.

resource.name: GraphDefinition
resource.description: A formal computable definition of a graph of resources - that is, a coherent set of resources that form a graph by following references. The Graph Definition resource defines a set and makes rules about the set.

property.name: id
property.description: The logical id of the resource, as used in the URL for the resource. Once assigned, this value never changes.

property.name: meta
property.description: The metadata about the resource. This is content that is maintained by the infrastructure. Changes to the content might not always be associated with version changes to the resource.

property.name: implicitRules
property.description: A reference to a set of rules that were followed when the resource was constructed, and which must be understood when processing the content. Often, this is a reference to an implementation guide that defines the special rules along with other profiles etc.

property.name: language
property.description: The base language in which the resource is written.

property.name: text
property.description: A human-readable narrative that contains a summary of the resource and can be used to represent the content of the resource to a human. The narrative need not encode all the structured data, but is required to contain sufficient detail to make it "clinically safe" for a human to just read the narrative. Resource definitions may define what content should be represented in the narrative to ensure clinical safety.

property.name: url
property.description: An absolute URI that is used to identify this graph definition when it is referenced in a specification, model, design or an instance; also called its canonical identifier. This SHOULD be globally unique and SHOULD be a literal address at which an authoritative instance of this graph definition is (or will be) published. This URL can be the target of a canonical reference. It SHALL remain the same when the graph definition is stored on different servers.

property.name: identifier
property.description: A formal identifier that is used to identify this GraphDefinition when it is represented in other formats, or referenced in a specification, model, design or an instance.

property.name: version
property.description: The identifier that is used to identify this version of the graph definition when it is referenced in a specification, model, design or instance. This is an arbitrary value managed by the graph definition author and is not expected to be globally unique. For example, it might be a timestamp (e.g. yyyymmdd) if a managed version is not available. There is also no expectation that versions can be placed in a lexicographical sequence.

property.name: versionAlgorithm
property.description: Indicates the mechanism used to compare versions to determine which is more current.

property.name: name
property.description: A natural language name identifying the graph definition. This name should be usable as an identifier for the module by machine processing applications such as code generation.

property.name: title
property.description: A short, descriptive, user-friendly title for the capability statement.

property.name: status
property.description: The status of this graph definition. Enables tracking the life-cycle of the content.

property.name: experimental
property.description: A Boolean value to indicate that this graph definition is authored for testing purposes (or education/evaluation/marketing) and is not intended to be used for genuine usage.

property.name: date
property.description: The date (and optionally time) when the graph definition was last significantly changed. The date must change when the business version changes and it must change if the status code changes. In addition, it should change when the substantive content of the graph definition changes.

property.name: publisher
property.description: The name of the organization or individual responsible for the release and ongoing maintenance of the graph definition.

property.name: contact
property.description: Contact details to assist a user in finding and communicating with the publisher.

property.name: description
property.description: A free text natural language description of the graph definition from a consumers perspective.

property.name: useContext
property.description: The content was developed with a focus and intent of supporting the contexts that are listed. These contexts may be general categories (gender, age, ...) or may be references to specific programs (insurance plans, studies, ...) and may be used to assist with indexing and searching for appropriate graph definition instances.

property.name: jurisdiction
property.description: A legal or geographic region in which the graph definition is intended to be used.

property.name: purpose
property.description: Explanation of why this graph definition is needed and why it has been designed as it has.

resource.name: Group

property.name: identifier

property.name: active

property.name: type
property.description: Identifies the broad classification of the kind of resources the group includes.

property.name: membership
property.description: Basis for membership in the Group:* definitional: The Group.characteristics specified are both necessary and sufficient to determine membership. All entities that meet the criteria are considered to be members of the group, whether referenced by the group or not. If members are present, they are individuals that happen to be known as meeting the Group.characteristics. The list cannot be presumed to be complete.* enumerated: The Group.characteristics are necessary but not sufficient to determine membership. Membership is determined by being listed as one of the Group.member.

property.name: code
property.description: Provides a specific type of resource the group includes; e.g. "cow", "syringe", etc.

property.name: name
property.description: A label assigned to the group for human identification and communication.

property.name: description
property.description: Explanation of what the group represents and how it is intended to be used.

property.name: quantity

property.name: exclude
property.description: If true, indicates the characteristic is one that is NOT held by members of the group.

property.name: period
property.description: The period over which the characteristic is tested; e.g. the patient had an operation during the month of June.

property.name: id
property.description: Unique id for the element within a resource (for internal references). This may be any string value that does not contain spaces.

property.name: entity
property.description: A reference to the entity that is a member of the group. Must be consistent with Group.type. If the entity is another group, then the type must be the same.

property.name: period
property.description: The period that the member was in the group, if known.

property.name: inactive
property.description: A flag to indicate that the member is no longer in the group, but previously may have been a member.

codeset.name: GroupType

code.description: Group contains "person" Patient resources.

code.name: Relatedperson

code.name: Specimen
