property.name: url
property.description: An absolute URI that is used to identify this questionnaire when it is referenced in a specification, model, design or an instance; also called its canonical identifier. This SHOULD be globally unique and SHOULD be a literal address at which an authoritative instance of this questionnaire is (or will be) published. This URL can be the target of a canonical reference. It SHALL remain the same when the questionnaire is stored on different servers.

property.name: identifier
property.description: A formal identifier that is used to identify this questionnaire when it is represented in other formats, or referenced in a specification, model, design or an instance.

property.name: version
property.description: The identifier that is used to identify this version of the questionnaire when it is referenced in a specification, model, design or instance. This is an arbitrary value managed by the questionnaire author and is not expected to be globally unique. For example, it might be a timestamp (e.g. yyyymmdd) if a managed version is not available. There is also no expectation that versions can be placed in a lexicographical sequence.

property.name: versionAlgorithm
property.description: Indicates the mechanism used to compare versions to determine which is more current.

property.name: name
property.description: A natural language name identifying the questionnaire. This name should be usable as an identifier for the module by machine processing applications such as code generation.

property.name: title
property.description: A short, descriptive, user-friendly title for the questionnaire.

property.name: derivedFrom
property.description: The URL of a Questionnaire that this Questionnaire is based on.

property.name: status
property.description: The current state of this questionnaire.

property.name: experimental
property.description: A Boolean value to indicate that this questionnaire is authored for testing purposes (or education/evaluation/marketing) and is not intended for genuine usage.

property.name: subjectType
property.description: The types of subjects that can be the subject of responses created for the questionnaire.

property.name: date
property.description: The date (and optionally time) when the questionnaire was last significantly changed. The date must change when the business version changes and it must change if the status code changes. In addition, it should change when the substantive content of the questionnaire changes.

property.name: publisher
property.description: The name of the organization or individual responsible for the release and ongoing maintenance of the questionnaire.

property.name: contact
property.description: Contact details to assist a user in finding and communicating with the publisher.

property.name: description
property.description: A free text natural language description of the questionnaire from a consumers perspective.

property.name: useContext
property.description: The content was developed with a focus and intent of supporting the contexts that are listed. These contexts may be general categories (gender, age, ...) or may be references to specific programs (insurance plans, studies, ...) and may be used to assist with indexing and searching for appropriate questionnaires.

property.name: jurisdiction
property.description: A legal or geographic region in which the questionnaire is intended to be used.

property.name: purpose
property.description: Explanation of why this questionnaire is needed and why it has been designed as it has.

property.name: copyright
property.description: A copyright statement relating to the questionnaire and/or its contents. Copyright statements are generally legal restrictions on the use and publishing of the questionnaire.

property.name: copyrightLabel
property.description: A short string (lower than50 characters), suitable for inclusion in a page footer that identifies the copyright holder, effective period, and optionally whether rights are resctricted. (e.g. All rights reserved, Some rights reserved).

property.name: approvalDate
property.description: The date on which the resource content was approved by the publisher. Approval happens once when the content is officially approved for usage.

property.name: lastReviewDate
property.description: The date on which the resource content was last reviewed. Review happens periodically after approval but does not change the original approval date.

property.name: effectivePeriod
property.description: The period during which the questionnaire content was or is planned to be in active use.

property.name: code
property.description: An identifier for this collection of questions in a particular terminology such as LOINC.

property.name: item
property.description: A particular question, question grouping or display text that is part of the questionnaire.

property.name: id
property.description: Unique id for the element within a resource (for internal references). This may be any string value that does not contain spaces.

property.name: linkId
property.description: An identifier that is unique within the Questionnaire allowing linkage to the equivalent item in a QuestionnaireResponse resource.

property.name: definition
property.description: This element is a URI that refers to an [ElementDefinition](elementdefinition.html) or to an [ObservationDefinition](observationdefinition.html) that provides information about this item, including information that might otherwise be included in the instance of the Questionnaire resource. A detailed description of the construction of the URI is shown in [Comments](questionnaire.html#definition), below.

property.name: code
property.description: A terminology code that corresponds to this group or question (e.g. a code from LOINC, which defines many questions and answers).

property.name: prefix
property.description: A short label for a particular group, question or set of display text within the questionnaire used for reference by the individual completing the questionnaire.

property.name: text
property.description: The name of a section, the text of a question or text content for a display item.

property.name: type
property.description: The type of questionnaire item this is - whether text for display, a grouping of other items or a particular type of data to be captured (string, integer, Coding, etc.).

property.name: enableWhen
property.description: A constraint indicating that this item should only be enabled (displayed/allow answers to be captured) when the specified condition is true.

property.name: enableBehavior
property.description: Controls how multiple enableWhen values are interpreted - whether all or any must be true.

property.name: disabledDisplay
property.description: Indicates if and how items that are disabled (because enableWhen evaluates to false) should be displayed.

property.name: required
property.description: An indication, if true, that the item must be present in a "completed" QuestionnaireResponse. If false, the item may be skipped when answering the questionnaire.

property.name: repeats
property.description: An indication, if true, that a QuestionnaireResponse for this item may include multiple answers associated with a single instance of this item (for question-type items) or multiple repetitions of the item (for group-type items).

property.name: readOnly
property.description: An indication, when true, that the value cannot be changed by a human respondent to the Questionnaire.

property.name: maxLength
property.description: The maximum number of characters that are permitted in the answer to be considered a "valid" QuestionnaireResponse.

property.name: answerConstraint
property.description: For items that have a defined set of allowed answers (via answerOption or answerValueSet), indicates whether values *other* than those specified can be selected.

property.name: answerValueSet
property.description: A reference to a value set containing a list of values representing permitted answers for a question.

property.name: answerOption
property.description: One of the permitted answers for the question.

property.name: initial
property.description: One or more values that should be pre-populated in the answer when initially rendering the questionnaire for user input.

property.name: item
property.description: Text, questions and other groups to be nested beneath a question or group.

property.name: id
property.description: Unique id for the element within a resource (for internal references). This may be any string value that does not contain spaces.

property.name: question
property.description: The linkId for the question whose answer (or lack of answer) governs whether this item is enabled.

property.name: operator
property.description: Specifies the criteria by which the question is enabled.

property.name: answer
property.description: A value that the referenced question is tested using the specified operator in order for the item to be enabled. If there are multiple answers, a match on any of the answers suffices. If different behavior is desired (all must match, at least 2 must match, etc.), consider using the enableWhenExpression extension.

property.name: id
property.description: Unique id for the element within a resource (for internal references). This may be any string value that does not contain spaces.

property.name: value
property.description: A potential answer thats allowed as the answer to this question.

property.name: initialSelected
property.description: Indicates whether the answer value is selected when the list of possible answers is initially shown.

property.name: id
property.description: Unique id for the element within a resource (for internal references). This may be any string value that does not contain spaces.

property.name: value
property.description: The actual value to for an initial answer.

codeset.name: QuestionnaireItemType
codeset.description: Distinguishes groups from questions and display text and indicates data type for questions.

code.name: Group
code.description: An item with no direct answer but should have at least one child item.

code.name: Display
code.description: Text for display that will not capture an answer or have child items.

code.name: Boolean
code.description: Question with a yes/no answer (valueBoolean).

code.name: Decimal
code.description: Question with is a real number answer (valueDecimal). There is an extension http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/questionnaire-unit that can be used to computably convey the unit of measure associated with the answer for use when performing data extraction to an element of type Quantity.

code.name: Integer
code.description: Question with an integer answer (valueInteger). There is an extension http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/questionnaire-unit that can be used to computably convey the unit of measure associated with the answer for use when performing data extraction to an element of type Quantity.

code.name: Date
code.description: Question with a date answer (valueDate).

code.name: DateTime
code.description: Question with a date and time answer (valueDateTime).

code.name: Time
code.description: Question with a time (hour:minute:second) answer independent of date. (valueTime).

code.name: String
code.description: Question with a short (few words to short sentence) free-text entry answer (valueString). Strings SHOULD NOT contain carriage return or newline characters. If multi-line answers are needed, use the text type.

code.name: Text
code.description: Question with a long (potentially multi-paragraph) free-text entry answer (valueString).

code.name: Url
code.description: Question with a URL (website, FTP site, etc.) answer (valueUri).

code.name: Coding
code.description: Question with a Coding - generally drawn from a list of possible answers (valueCoding)

code.name: Attachment
code.description: Question with binary content such as an image, PDF, etc. as an answer (valueAttachment).

code.name: Reference
code.description: Question with a reference to another resource (practitioner, organization, etc.) as an answer (valueReference).

code.name: Quantity
code.description: Question with a combination of a numeric value and unit as an answer. (valueSimpleQuantity) There are two extensions (http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/questionnaire-unitOption and http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/questionnaire-unitValueSet) that can be used to define what unit should be selected for the Quantity.code and Quantity.system.

codeset.name: QuestionnaireItemOperator
codeset.description: The criteria by which a question is enabled.

code.name: Exists
code.description: True if the determination of whether an answer exists for the question is equal to the enableWhen answer (which must be a boolean).

code.name: Equal
code.description: True if at least one answer has a value that is equal to the enableWhen answer.

code.name: NotEqual
code.description: True if no answer has a value that is equal to the enableWhen answer.

code.name: GreaterThan
code.description: True if at least one answer has a value that is greater than the enableWhen answer.

code.name: LessThan
code.description: True if at least one answer has a value that is less than the enableWhen answer.

code.name: GreaterOrEqual
code.description: True if at least one answer has a value that is greater or equal to the enableWhen answer.

code.name: LessOrEqual
code.description: True if at least one answer has a value that is less or equal to the enableWhen answer.

codeset.name: EnableWhenBehavior
codeset.description: Controls how multiple enableWhen values are interpreted - whether all or any must be true.

code.name: All
code.description: Enable the question when all the enableWhen criteria are satisfied.

code.name: Any
code.description: Enable the question when any of the enableWhen criteria are satisfied.

codeset.name: QuestionnaireItemDisabledDisplay
codeset.description: Codes that guide the display of disabled questionnaire items

code.name: Hidden
code.description: The item (and its children) should not be visible to the user at all.

code.name: Protected
code.description: The item (and possibly its children) should not be selectable or editable but should still be visible - to allow the user to see what questions *could* have been completed had other answers caused the item to be enabled.

codeset.name: QuestionnaireAnswerConstraint
codeset.description: Codes that describe the types of constraints possible on a question item that has a list of permitted answers

code.name: OptionsOnly
code.description: Only values listed as answerOption or in the expansion of the answerValueSet are permitted

code.name: OptionsOrType
code.description: In addition to the values listed as answerOption or in the expansion of the answerValueSet, any other values that correspond to the specified item.type are permitted

code.name: OptionsOrString
code.description: In addition to the values listed as answerOption or in the expansion of the answerValueSet, free-text strings are permitted. Answers will have a type of string.

resource.name: QuestionnaireResponse
resource.description: A structured set of questions and their answers. The questions are ordered and grouped into coherent subsets, corresponding to the structure of the grouping of the questionnaire being responded to.

property.name: id
property.description: The logical id of the resource, as used in the URL for the resource. Once assigned, this value never changes.

property.name: meta
property.description: The metadata about the resource. This is content that is maintained by the infrastructure. Changes to the content might not always be associated with version changes to the resource.

property.name: implicitRules
property.description: A reference to a set of rules that were followed when the resource was constructed, and which must be understood when processing the content. Often, this is a reference to an implementation guide that defines the special rules along with other profiles etc.

property.name: language
property.description: The base language in which the resource is written.

property.name: text
property.description: A human-readable narrative that contains a summary of the resource and can be used to represent the content of the resource to a human. The narrative need not encode all the structured data, but is required to contain sufficient detail to make it "clinically safe" for a human to just read the narrative. Resource definitions may define what content should be represented in the narrative to ensure clinical safety.

property.name: identifier
property.description: Business identifiers assigned to this questionnaire response by the performer and/or other systems. These identifiers remain constant as the resource is updated and propagates from server to server.

property.name: basedOn
property.description: A plan, proposal or order that is fulfilled in whole or in part by this questionnaire response. For example, a ServiceRequest seeking an intake assessment or a decision support recommendation to assess for post-partum depression.

property.name: partOf
property.description: A procedure or observation that this questionnaire was performed as part of the execution of. For example, the surgery a checklist was executed as part of.

property.name: questionnaire
property.description: The Questionnaire that defines and organizes the questions for which answers are being provided.

property.name: status
property.description: The current state of the questionnaire response.

property.name: subject
property.description: The subject of the questionnaire response. This could be a patient, organization, practitioner, device, etc. This is who/what the answers apply to, but is not necessarily the source of information.

property.name: encounter
property.description: The Encounter during which this questionnaire response was created or to which the creation of this record is tightly associated.

property.name: authored
property.description: The date and/or time that this questionnaire response was last modified by the user - e.g. changing answers or revising status.

property.name: author
property.description: The individual or device that received the answers to the questions in the QuestionnaireResponse and recorded them in the system.

property.name: source
property.description: The individual or device that answered the questions about the subject.

property.name: item
property.description: A group or question item from the original questionnaire for which answers are provided.

property.name: id
property.description: Unique id for the element within a resource (for internal references). This may be any string value that does not contain spaces.

property.name: linkId
property.description: The item from the Questionnaire that corresponds to this item in the QuestionnaireResponse resource.

property.name: definition
property.description: A reference to an [ElementDefinition](elementdefinition.html) that provides the details for the item.

property.name: text
property.description: Text that is displayed above the contents of the group or as the text of the question being answered.

property.name: answer
property.description: The respondents answer(s) to the question.

property.name: item
property.description: Sub-questions, sub-groups or display items nested beneath a group.

property.name: id
property.description: Unique id for the element within a resource (for internal references). This may be any string value that does not contain spaces.

property.name: value
property.description: The answer (or one of the answers) provided by the respondent to the question.

property.name: item
property.description: Nested groups and/or questions found within this particular answer.

codeset.name: QuestionnaireResponseStatus
codeset.description: Lifecycle status of the questionnaire response.

code.name: InProgress
code.description: This QuestionnaireResponse has been partially filled out with answers but changes or additions are still expected to be made to it.

code.name: Completed
code.description: This QuestionnaireResponse has been filled out with answers and the current content is regarded as definitive.

code.name: Amended
code.description: This QuestionnaireResponse has been filled out with answers, then marked as complete, yet changes or additions have been made to it afterwards.

code.name: EnteredInError
code.description: This QuestionnaireResponse was entered in error and voided.

code.name: Stopped
code.description: This QuestionnaireResponse has been partially filled out with answers but has been abandoned. No subsequent changes can be made.

resource.name: RegulatedAuthorization
resource.description: Regulatory approval, clearance or licencing related to a regulated product, treatment, facility or activity that is cited in a guidance, regulation, rule or legislative act. An example is Market Authorization relating to a Medicinal Product.

property.name: id
property.description: The logical id of the resource, as used in the URL for the resource. Once assigned, this value never changes.

property.name: meta
property.description: The metadata about the resource. This is content that is maintained by the infrastructure. Changes to the content might not always be associated with version changes to the resource.

property.name: implicitRules
property.description: A reference to a set of rules that were followed when the resource was constructed, and which must be understood when processing the content. Often, this is a reference to an implementation guide that defines the special rules along with other profiles etc.

property.name: language
property.description: The base language in which the resource is written.

property.name: text
property.description: A human-readable narrative that contains a summary of the resource and can be used to represent the content of the resource to a human. The narrative need not encode all the structured data, but is required to contain sufficient detail to make it "clinically safe" for a human to just read the narrative. Resource definitions may define what content should be represented in the narrative to ensure clinical safety.

property.name: identifier
property.description: Business identifier for the authorization, typically assigned by the authorizing body.

property.name: subject
property.description: The product type, treatment, facility or activity that is being authorized.

property.name: type
property.description: Overall type of this authorization, for example drug marketing approval, orphan drug designation.

property.name: description
property.description: General textual supporting information.

property.name: region
property.description: The territory (e.g., country, jurisdiction etc.) in which the authorization has been granted.

property.name: status
property.description: The status that is authorised e.g. approved. Intermediate states and actions can be tracked with cases and applications.

property.name: statusDate
property.description: The date at which the current status was assigned.

property.name: validityPeriod
property.description: The time period in which the regulatory approval, clearance or licencing is in effect. As an example, a Marketing Authorization includes the date of authorization and/or an expiration date.

property.name: indication
property.description: Condition for which the use of the regulated product applies.

property.name: intendedUse
property.description: The intended use of the product, e.g. prevention, treatment, diagnosis.

property.name: basis
property.description: The legal or regulatory framework against which this authorization is granted, or other reasons for it.

property.name: holder
property.description: The organization that has been granted this authorization, by some authoritative body (the regulator).

property.name: regulator
property.description: The regulatory authority or authorizing body granting the authorization. For example, European Medicines Agency (EMA), Food and Drug Administration (FDA), Health Canada (HC), etc.

property.name: attachedDocument
property.description: Additional information or supporting documentation about the authorization.

property.name: case
property.description: The case or regulatory procedure for granting or amending a regulated authorization. An authorization is granted in response to submissions/applications by those seeking authorization. A case is the administrative process that deals with the application(s) that relate to this and assesses them. Note: This area is subject to ongoing review and the workgroup is seeking implementer feedback on its use (see link at bottom of page).

property.name: id
property.description: Unique id for the element within a resource (for internal references). This may be any string value that does not contain spaces.

property.name: identifier
property.description: Identifier by which this case can be referenced.

property.name: type
property.description: The defining type of case.

property.name: status
property.description: The status associated with the case.

property.name: date
property.description: Relevant date for this case.

property.name: application
property.description: A regulatory submission from an organization to a regulator, as part of an assessing case. Multiple applications may occur over time, with more or different information to support or modify the submission or the authorization. The applications can be considered as steps within the longer running case or procedure for this authorization process.

resource.name: RelatedPerson
resource.description: Information about a person that is involved in a patients health or the care for a patient, but who is not the target of healthcare, nor has a formal responsibility in the care process.

property.name: id
property.description: The logical id of the resource, as used in the URL for the resource. Once assigned, this value never changes.

property.name: meta
property.description: The metadata about the resource. This is content that is maintained by the infrastructure. Changes to the content might not always be associated with version changes to the resource.

property.name: implicitRules
property.description: A reference to a set of rules that were followed when the resource was constructed, and which must be understood when processing the content. Often, this is a reference to an implementation guide that defines the special rules along with other profiles etc.

property.name: language
property.description: The base language in which the resource is written.

property.name: text
property.description: A human-readable narrative that contains a summary of the resource and can be used to represent the content of the resource to a human. The narrative need not encode all the structured data, but is required to contain sufficient detail to make it "clinically safe" for a human to just read the narrative. Resource definitions may define what content should be represented in the narrative to ensure clinical safety.

property.name: identifier
property.description: Identifier for a person within a particular scope.

property.name: active
property.description: Whether this related person record is in active use.

property.name: patient
property.description: The patient this person is related to.

property.name: relationship
property.description: The nature of the relationship between the related person and the patient.

property.name: name
property.description: A name associated with the person.

property.name: telecom
property.description: A contact detail for the person, e.g. a telephone number or an email address.

property.name: gender
property.description: Administrative Gender - the gender that the person is considered to have for administration and record keeping purposes.

property.name: birthDate
property.description: The date on which the related person was born.

property.name: address
property.description: Address where the related person can be contacted or visited.

property.name: photo
property.description: Image of the person.

property.name: period
property.description: The period of time during which this relationship is or was active. If there are no dates defined, then the interval is unknown.

property.name: communication
property.description: A language which may be used to communicate with the related person about the patients health.

property.name: id
property.description: Unique id for the element within a resource (for internal references). This may be any string value that does not contain spaces.

property.name: language
property.description: The ISO-639-1 alpha 2 code in lower case for the language, optionally followed by a hyphen and the ISO-3166-1 alpha 2 code for the region in upper case; e.g. "en" for English, or "en-US" for American English versus "en-AU" for Australian English.

property.name: preferred
property.description: Indicates whether or not the related person prefers this language (over other languages he or she masters up a certain level).

resource.name: RequestOrchestration
resource.description: A set of related requests that can be used to capture intended activities that have inter-dependencies such as "give this medication after that one".

property.name: id
property.description: The logical id of the resource, as used in the URL for the resource. Once assigned, this value never changes.

property.name: meta
property.description: The metadata about the resource. This is content that is maintained by the infrastructure. Changes to the content might not always be associated with version changes to the resource.

property.name: implicitRules
property.description: A reference to a set of rules that were followed when the resource was constructed, and which must be understood when processing the content. Often, this is a reference to an implementation guide that defines the special rules along with other profiles etc.

property.name: language
property.description: The base language in which the resource is written.

property.name: text
property.description: A human-readable narrative that contains a summary of the resource and can be used to represent the content of the resource to a human. The narrative need not encode all the structured data, but is required to contain sufficient detail to make it "clinically safe" for a human to just read the narrative. Resource definitions may define what content should be represented in the narrative to ensure clinical safety.

property.name: identifier
property.description: Allows a service to provide a unique, business identifier for the request.

property.name: instantiatesCanonical
property.description: A canonical URL referencing a FHIR-defined protocol, guideline, orderset or other definition that is adhered to in whole or in part by this request.

property.name: instantiatesUri
property.description: A URL referencing an externally defined protocol, guideline, orderset or other definition that is adhered to in whole or in part by this request.

property.name: basedOn
property.description: A plan, proposal or order that is fulfilled in whole or in part by this request.

property.name: replaces
property.description: Completed or terminated request(s) whose function is taken by this new request.

property.name: groupIdentifier
property.description: A shared identifier common to multiple independent Request instances that were activated/authorized more or less simultaneously by a single author. The presence of the same identifier on each request ties those requests together and may have business ramifications in terms of reporting of results, billing, etc. E.g. a requisition number shared by a set of lab tests ordered together, or a prescription number shared by all meds ordered at one time.

property.name: status
property.description: The current state of the request. For request orchestrations, the status reflects the status of all the requests in the orchestration.

property.name: intent
property.description: Indicates the level of authority/intentionality associated with the request and where the request fits into the workflow chain.

property.name: priority
property.description: Indicates how quickly the request should be addressed with respect to other requests.

property.name: code
property.description: A code that identifies what the overall request orchestration is.

property.name: subject
property.description: The subject for which the request orchestration was created.

property.name: encounter
property.description: Describes the context of the request orchestration, if any.

property.name: authoredOn
property.description: Indicates when the request orchestration was created.

property.name: author
property.description: Provides a reference to the author of the request orchestration.

property.name: reason
property.description: Describes the reason for the request orchestration in coded or textual form.

property.name: goal
property.description: Goals that are intended to be achieved by following the requests in this RequestOrchestration.

property.name: note
property.description: Provides a mechanism to communicate additional information about the response.

property.name: action
property.description: The actions, if any, produced by the evaluation of the artifact.

property.name: id
property.description: Unique id for the element within a resource (for internal references). This may be any string value that does not contain spaces.

property.name: linkId
property.description: The linkId of the action from the PlanDefinition that corresponds to this action in the RequestOrchestration resource.

property.name: prefix
property.description: A user-visible prefix for the action. For example a section or item numbering such as 1. or A.

property.name: title
property.description: The title of the action displayed to a user.

property.name: description
property.description: A short description of the action used to provide a summary to display to the user.

property.name: textEquivalent
property.description: A text equivalent of the action to be performed. This provides a human-interpretable description of the action when the definition is consumed by a system that might not be capable of interpreting it dynamically.

property.name: priority
property.description: Indicates how quickly the action should be addressed with respect to other actions.

property.name: code
property.description: A code that provides meaning for the action or action group. For example, a section may have a LOINC code for a section of a documentation template.

property.name: documentation
property.description: Didactic or other informational resources associated with the action that can be provided to the CDS recipient. Information resources can include inline text commentary and links to web resources.

property.name: goal
property.description: Goals that are intended to be achieved by following the requests in this action.

property.name: condition
property.description: An expression that describes applicability criteria, or start/stop conditions for the action.

property.name: input
property.description: Defines input data requirements for the action.

property.name: output
property.description: Defines the outputs of the action, if any.

property.name: relatedAction
property.description: A relationship to another action such as "before" or "30-60 minutes after start of".

property.name: timing
property.description: An optional value describing when the action should be performed.

property.name: location
property.description: Identifies the facility where the action will occur; e.g. home, hospital, specific clinic, etc.

property.name: participant
property.description: The participant that should perform or be responsible for this action.

property.name: type
property.description: The type of action to perform (create, update, remove).

property.name: groupingBehavior
property.description: Defines the grouping behavior for the action and its children.

property.name: selectionBehavior
property.description: Defines the selection behavior for the action and its children.

property.name: requiredBehavior
property.description: Defines expectations around whether an action is required.

property.name: precheckBehavior
property.description: Defines whether the action should usually be preselected.

property.name: cardinalityBehavior
property.description: Defines whether the action can be selected multiple times.

property.name: resource
property.description: The resource that is the target of the action (e.g. CommunicationRequest).

property.name: definition
property.description: A reference to an ActivityDefinition that describes the action to be taken in detail, a PlanDefinition that describes a series of actions to be taken, a Questionnaire that should be filled out, a SpecimenDefinition describing a specimen to be collected, or an ObservationDefinition that specifies what observation should be captured.

property.name: transform
property.description: A reference to a StructureMap resource that defines a transform that can be executed to produce the intent resource using the ActivityDefinition instance as the input.

property.name: dynamicValue
property.description: Customizations that should be applied to the statically defined resource. For example, if the dosage of a medication must be computed based on the patients weight, a customization would be used to specify an expression that calculated the weight, and the path on the resource that would contain the result.

property.name: action
property.description: Sub actions.

property.name: id

property.name: kind
property.description: The kind of condition.

property.name: expression

property.name: id
property.description: Unique id for the element within a resource (for internal references). This may be any string value that does not contain spaces.

property.name: endRelationship
property.description: The relationship of the end of this action to the related action.

property.name: offset
property.description: A duration or range of durations to apply to the relationship. For example, 30-60 minutes before.

property.name: id

resource.name: ResearchStudy
resource.description: A scientific study of nature that sometimes includes processes involved in health and disease. For example, clinical trials are research studies that involve people. These studies may be related to new ways to screen, prevent, diagnose, and treat disease. They may also study certain outcomes and certain groups of people by looking at data collected in the past or future.

property.description: The logical id of the resource, as used in the URL for the resource. Once assigned, this value never changes.

Resource definitions may define what content should be represented in the narrative to ensure clinical safety.

property.name: identifier
property.description: Identifiers assigned to this research study by the sponsor or other systems.

property.name: version
property.description: The business version for the study record.

property.name: name
property.description: Name for this study (computer friendly).

property.name: title
property.description: The human readable name of the research study.

property.name: label
property.description: Additional names for the study.

property.name: protocol
property.description: The set of steps expected to be performed as part of the execution of the study.

property.name: partOf
property.description: A larger research study of which this particular study is a component or step.

property.name: relatedArtifact
property.description: Citations, references, URLs and other related documents. When using relatedArtifact to share URLs, the relatedArtifact.type will often be set to one of "documentation" or "supported-with" and the URL value will often be in relatedArtifact.document.url but another possible location is relatedArtifact.resource when it is a canonical URL.

property.name: date
property.description: The date (and optionally time) when the ResearchStudy Resource was last significantly changed. The date must change when the business version changes and it must change if the status code changes. In addition, it should change when the substantive content of the ResearchStudy Resource changes.

property.name: status
property.description: The publication state of the resource (not of the study).

property.description: The type of study based upon the intent of the study activities. A classification of the intent of the study.

property.name: phase
property.description: The stage in the progression of a therapy from initial experimental use in humans in clinical trials to post-market evaluation.

property.name: studyDesign
property.description: Codes categorizing the type of study such as investigational vs. observational, type of blinding, type of randomization, safety vs. efficacy, etc.

property.name: focus
property.description: The medication(s), food(s), therapy(ies), device(s) or other concerns or interventions that the study is seeking to gain more information about.

property.name: condition
property.description: The condition that is the focus of the study. For example, In a study to examine risk factors for Lupus, might have as an inclusion criterion "healthy volunteer", but the target condition code would be a Lupus SNOMED code.

property.name: keyword
property.description: Key terms to aid in searching for or filtering the study.

property.name: region
property.description: A country, state or other area where the study is taking place rather than its precise geographic location or address.

property.name: descriptionSummary
property.description: A brief text for explaining the study.

property.name: description
property.description: A detailed and human-readable narrative of the study. E.g., study abstract.

property.name: period
property.description: Identifies the start date and the expected (or actual, depending on status) end date for the study.

property.name: site
property.description: A facility in which study activities are conducted.

property.name: note
property.description: Comments made about the study by the performer, subject or other participants.

property.name: classifier
property.description: Additional grouping mechanism or categorization of a research study. Example: FDA regulated device, FDA regulated drug, MPG Paragraph 23b (a German legal requirement), IRB-exempt, etc. Implementation Note: do not use the classifier element to support existing semantics that are already supported thru explicit elements in the resource.

property.name: associatedParty
property.description: Sponsors, collaborators, and other parties.

property.name: progressStatus
property.description: Status of study with time for that status.

property.name: whyStopped
property.description: A description and/or code explaining the premature termination of the study.

property.name: recruitment
property.description: Target or actual group of participants enrolled in study.

property.name: comparisonGroup
property.description: Describes an expected event or sequence of events for one of the subjects of a study. E.g. for a living subject: exposure to drug A, wash-out, exposure to drug B, wash-out, follow-up. E.g. for a stability study: {store sample from lot A at 25 degrees for 1 month}, {store sample from lot A at 40 degrees for 1 month}.

property.name: objective
property.description: A goal that the study is aiming to achieve in terms of a scientific question to be answered by the analysis of data collected during the study.

property.name: outcomeMeasure
property.description: An "outcome measure", "endpoint", "effect measure" or "measure of effect" is a specific measurement or observation used to quantify the effect of experimental variables on the participants in a study, or for observational studies, to describe patterns of diseases or traits or associations with exposures, risk factors or treatment.

property.name: result
property.description: Link to one or more sets of results generated by the study. Could also link to a research registry holding the results such as ClinicalTrials.gov.

property.description: The parameter or characteristic being assessed as one of the values by which the study is assessed.

property.description: Description of the outcome.

property.description: The reason the risk assessment was performed.

property.description: Indicates the source data considered as part of the assessment (for example, FamilyHistory, Observations, Procedures, Conditions, etc.).

property.name: prediction
property.description: Describes the expected outcome for the subject.

property.name: mitigation
property.description: A description of the steps that might be taken to reduce the identified risk(s).

property.name: note
property.description: Additional comments about the risk assessment.

property.name: id
property.description: Unique id for the element within a resource (for internal references). This may be any string value that does not contain spaces.

property.description: One of the potential outcomes for the patient (e.g. remission, death, a particular condition).

property.name: probability
property.description: Indicates how likely the outcome is (in the specified timeframe).

property.name: qualitativeRisk
property.description: Indicates how likely the outcome is (in the specified timeframe), expressed as a qualitative value (e.g. low, medium, or high).

property.name: relativeRisk
property.description: Indicates the risk for this particular subject (with their specific characteristics) divided by the risk of the population in general. (Numbers greater than 1 = higher risk than the population, numbers less than 1 = lower risk.).

property.name: when
property.description: Indicates the period of time or age range of the subject to which the specified probability applies.

property.name: rationale
property.description: Additional information explaining the basis for the prediction.
